Donald Trump once again issued a grave threat to destroy the “entire country” of Iran during a phone call with a Fox News reporter on Sunday.

The president told Fox’s Trey Yingst that for him, the “question” was “if and when” it would be required to “blow the entire nation up” if Iran’s government did not submit to his demands.

It’s at least the second time the president has directly threatened to target Iran for widespread carnage, presumably affecting civilians. U.S. forces have already been criticized for strikes that have hit civilian areas, including a girls’ school in Minab in February, which killed 120 schoolchildren.

It comes as the president is facing staggeringly low polling on the war itself and is watching both his own popularity and the Republican Party’s sink like a stone as a result. A Fox News poll out this weekend found that 71 percent of Americans think that Trump lacks a plan to end the war altogether and new escalating conflicts between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia threaten to further disrupt the region.

“They better behave,” Yingst said the president told him of Iran’s government, adding that the choices included “wiping them out, letting Iran rot economically, or making a deal”.

open image in gallery Donald Trump once again threatened to destroy the entire country of Iran on Sunday ( Reuters )

But the U.S. and Iran seem no closer to a deal now than the two countries did in in July, when a ceasefire between U.S. and Iranian forces dissolved under a hail of Iranian attacks against shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

Meanwhile, the conflict seems to have reignited fighting between Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and the Saudi Arabian government, which is seeking to put an end to the years-long insurgency. U.S. and Houthi officials met one week ago in Oman to discuss the resumed hostilities, and affirmed that U.S. and neutral vessels would not be targeted by Houthi attacks as long as the U.S. remained on the sidelines.

open image in gallery A Houthi strike on Riyadh’s airport caused major flight disruptions Saturday ( Reuters )

Trump’s polling on the Iran war is disastrously low for the president, and worse for Republicans running in the approaching midterm elections. In the Fox News poll published last week, the president’s numbers are indefensible for Republicans: Six in ten voters say the war was the wrong decision, in hindsight, compared with just over a third who still support the president’s choice. Among those who believe the president lacks a clear strategy for extracting the U.S. from the conflict is four in ten Republicans and 83 percent of registered independents, according to the Fox poll.

The same survey found that more than four in ten voters believe the long-term effects of the war will make the U.S. less safe, compared to 32 percent who say it will make the country safer. The Trump administration’s stated reason for launching the strikes in January were to prohibit the reconstruction of Iran’s nuclear program, which the president said was “obliterated” in a previous round of strikes last summer and the administration has yet to prove was under redevelopment. The poll found that the war itself remains low on voters’ list of motivating factors ahead of the midterms though its related effects were not: Cost of living/inflation was the most-mentioned issue by poll respondents when asked about what was motivating their midterm vote. The economy and jobs were second.

Gas prices in the U.S. remain well north of $4 a gallon nationally, and fears of further conflict in and around the Strait of Hormuz have raised fears that prices will jump even higher before November.

open image in gallery Fuel prices in Great Neck, New York with less than two months to go before voters hit the polls ( Reuters )

Trump has said that Iran cannot be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon at any cost. But voters do not seem convinced that of the president’s explanation that Iran was close, or was attempting to resume efforts towards obtaining weaponizable nuclear material.

Six months into the Iran war, the costs of the conflict are mounting. Pentagon estimates indicate that the U.S. has spent tens of billions of dollars on the war already, even as the White House refuses to call it that — and U.S. stockpiles of critical defense munitions, such as Tomahawk cruise missiles and interceptor systems like THAAD units are dwindling to critical levels, posing problems not just for the U.S. efforts in Iran but around the world, where U.S. allies (including Ukraine) are reliant on supplies of those weapons.

The president’s previous threat to attack the “entire” country of Iran came on the eve of U.S. and Iranian officials striking the now-dead ceasefire agreement in early April.

open image in gallery Donald Trump is depicted on a billboard in Tehran as hostilities continue between the two nations ( Reuters )

At that time, Trump warned on Truth Social that “a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again. I don’t want that to happen, but it probably will.” His threats were taken by many of his critics as an admission that the U.S. government was considering targeting civilian areas, which would constitute war crimes.

Trump never followed through on that threat, and paused U.S. strikes on Iranian targets only hours later. In that same initial posting on Truth Social, the president wrote about how his administration was pursuing “regime change” in Iran, which his team has now reportedly largely abandoned as a goal and is only brought up by the president when he mentions the killing of Iran’s supreme leader, the Ayatollah Khamenei, in late February.

“La Bola Negra,” the Spanish queer epic about the intertwined lives of three gay men, won the People's Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sunday, confirming its status as a major Oscar contender.

TIFF's top award is voted on by festivalgoers, and it's become known as one of the most iron-clad Academy Awards predictors. Since 2012, all but one winner of the People's Choice Award has gone on to score a best-picture nomination at the Oscars. The lone exception was in 2024, when Mike Flanagan's Stephen King adaptation “The Life of Chuck” won the award. Last year, “Hamnet” won it and later landed eight Oscar nominations.

“La Bola Negra” is directed by the duo known as Los Javis — Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo. It was already a hit at the Cannes Film Festival, where “La Bola Negra” split the best director award with Paweł Pawlikowski for “Fatherland.”

Netflix acquired “La Bola Negra” out of Cannes and has launched a full awards campaign for the film. Netflix is also giving the film its longest theatrical release yet for the streamer. “La Bola Negra” opens in theaters Oct. 16 and begins streaming Dec. 2.

“This is a deeply personal film but it also carries a message of the importance and necessity of expressing who you are,” the Javis said in a statement Sunday. “Knowing that audiences connected with it and made it their own is the greatest gift we could receive.”

The first runner-up for the TIFF award was “I Play Rocky,” Peter Farrelly's comedy about the making of “Rocky.” Second runner-up was “Being Heumann,” Siân Heder's drama about disability rights pioneer Judy Heumann.

The festival also awards a People's Choice Award for international films. That went to “Elsinore,” starring Andrew Scott as Ian Charleson, the Scottish actor who performed “Hamlet” in London while suffering from AIDS. The first runner-up was “Possible Love,” Lee Chang-dong’s Korean drama about the trauma of mass layoffs. Second runner-up was “The Assassin(s),” a Korean procedural by Hur Jin-ho.

“Darlene Love: I Know Where I've Been,” a portrait of the 85-year-old vocalist, won TIFF's People's Choice Award for documentary. The festival's audience award for its Midnight Madness section went to “Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney,” a so-called “gonzo documentary” by Matthew Rankin about the former Canadian prime minister.

The 51st edition of TIFF draws to a close Sunday.

Australia's pioneering social media restrictions have been praised as "world-leading" by Apple Executive Chair Tim Cook, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated on Sunday following a meeting at the company's U.S. headquarters.

"Tim Cook gave us a lot of time this morning. He regards the work that we’ve done on social media to be world-leading," Albanese said in televised comments from Apple Park, California, broadcast in Australia on Sunday.

Australia advanced its efforts to improve digital safety this month by introducing a plan allowing social media users to choose the content shown on their feeds.

In December, Australia became the first nation to ban social media for children under 16. Other governments have followed suit this year, with the European Commission being the latest to propose a ban for children under 13.

When asked to comment on Albanese's remarks, an Apple spokesperson pointed to a post by Cook on X, noting he was grateful to share with Albanese "some of our newest innovations, including strong and intuitive controls to help keep kids safe online."

( Getty/iStock )

Cook recently stepped down as Apple CEO after a 15-year tenure in the role.

The visit by Albanese to the U.S. comes as tech leaders remain divided over how fast companies ought to develop increasingly powerful technology, while an AI safety debate continues across Silicon Valley.

Albanese emphasized that AI brings risks that must be managed.

"There is a need for a discussion about what the global framework is for the rollout of AI, because it is moving very quickly, and we need to make sure that humans remain in control," he told reporters, according to an official transcript.

The Australian leader's stance contrasts with that of President Donald Trump, who has downplayed concerns surrounding AI and argued that further regulation is unnecessary.

News.title: Isak makes difference for Liverpool on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
News.content:
The first shot Alexander Isak tried was a threat to low-flying pigeons. During a frustrating first half, when he barely got a touch, his one sight of goal ended with him slashing his attempt high and wide.

Then, early in the second half, came a cross that was sliced so badly, weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy. Isak had wriggled to the byline but, again, his contact sent the ball miles away from where it should have been.

Was it going to be one of those afternoons? The Swede had not even made it into Bournemouth’s penalty area in the opening 45 minutes and it looked for all the world that the narrative was going to be wearily familiar. But, then, everything changed: third time lucky, as the saying goes.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards, his fourth goal in four Premier League games.

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

News.title: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash
News.content:
Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Roy Keane looks absolutely fuming as he watches former club in dismal derby defeat
Sports.content:
Next

FUMING Roy Keane watched Celtic succumb to a gut-wrenching 1-0 Old Firm defeat.

The Manchester United legend sat gloomy-faced in the stands of Celtic Park as his former side and boyhood club failed to score.



This comes a week after United saw the same fate in their Manchester derby.

Ryan Naderi’s first-half strike proved to be the only goal of the game for Derek McInnes’ side in a week with TWO Old Firm derbies – and two Rangers victories.



The visitors had an immediate opportunity to double their lead.

Luckily for Celtic, it skimmed just wide.

Rangers kept knocking and fans were forced to hold their breath after Olwethu Makhanya’s superb effort after it flew into the top corner – before officials ruled it out for hand-ball.

The Bhoys never looked like extending their Premiership winning streak to seven.

Instead, the loss was chalked off as their first league defeat since Dundee United beat them at Tannadice in March.

The Rangers win shortened the gap between the Scottish Premiership rivals to only TWO points as both sides head into the three-week international break.

Martin O’Neill’s future has been left hanging in the balance, having lost three times in just seven days.

The Ibrox thumping came first last Sunday, where Dan Neil’s brace and Kevin Kelsy’s effort secured a 3-0 League Cup victory.

A Europa League 3-1 defeat followed on Thursday against Ferencvaros, before their defeat today.

Former Ireland skipper Keane made ten appearances for his boyhood club Celtic in 2006 – scoring one goal, a shot from 20 yards out in a 2–1 league win over Falkirk.



The 55-year-old only competed in one Old Firm derby, but he did lead them to a 1-0 win through Maciej Zurawski’s early goal.

His Celtic side went on to lift the Scottish Premier League title and Scottish League Cup before hanging up his boots.

DIEGO SIMEONE was fuming after Julian Alvarez was booed by his own fans while being substituted on during the Madrid Derby.

The Argentina star was involved in a chaotic transfer saga in the summer window which saw him try to secure a move to rivals Barcelona.

Arsenal were also interested in his services, but Atletico held firm that they were not interested in selling him – especially to the defending Spanish champions.



Fans were not appreciative of his conduct during the strange standoff, jeering him earlier this season while the star was stopped from heading over to the fans by his team-mates.



And it seems even the mammoth occasion at the Metropolitano was not enough to overshadow the bad blood between the two parties.

Alvarez was brought on off the bench for Jonathan David after the Canadian gave his side a 2-0 advantage over their rivals.

But the 70,000-strong crowd where not in a forgiving mood, and brutally booed and whistled the star as he entered the field of play.



Manager Simeone was absolutely fuming with the gesture, with the antics hardly helping his side’s confidence as they looked to defend their lead against Jose Mourinho’s men.

One commentator said: “Simeone is livid with the supporters.”

“In this stadium they do as they’re told by Simeone, and he’s made it clear his feelings that he thinks that they’re not doing the correct thing.”

Sports.title: Fans evacuated as Celtic supporters’ bus goes up in flames short distance away from stadium moments after Rangers clash

FANS had to be evacuated from a supporters’ bus that went on fire near Celtic Park after today’s Old Firm derby clash.

On the park Rangers took all three points with a 1-0 victory thanks to a goal from Ryan Naderi in the first half.



The Hoops supporters inside the ground booed their team off the pitch as Gers closed the gap at the top of the Premiership table to two points.

After the game there were worrying scenes on the A728 (Clyde Gateway) near to the Emirates Arena as a coach went up in flames as it made its way away from Parkhead.





The fire started from the rear of the vehicle but soon spread and plumes of thick black smoke carried high into the air.

All of the fans inside were quickly evacuated as emergency crews rushed to the incident in Glasgow’s east end.

Two fire engines arrived on the scene and it brought the busy road to a standstill at around 2.30pm this afternoon.

Fans gathered on the pavement next to a food vendor as firefighters tackled the blaze.



It’s understood the bus belonged to the Motherwell 9 in a Row CSC, who hire a bus from McLean’s Coaches of Airdrie.

Eventually the bus was loaded onto the back of a recovery lorry, with the back of the vehicle destroyed.

OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

Police Scotland confirmed there were no injuries.



McLean’s Coaches told The Scottish Sun: “We are aware of the incident involving one of our vehicles on the Clyde Gateway today.

“The vehicle has been recovered, and we are working with the relevant authorities and parties to establish exactly what happened. The cause of the fire has not yet been confirmed, so it would be inappropriate to speculate while enquiries are ongoing.

“Safety is our highest priority, and the vehicle will undergo a full investigation before any further steps are decided.”

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service have been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Leeds 0 Crystal Palace 0: Eagles denied crucial win by VAR as sides are forced to settle for bore draw
Sports.content:
Next

DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN’S goal-den run came to a frustrating end as Leeds were held by struggling Crystal Palace.

The in-form striker was chasing a sixth successive goal at Elland Road to match a record that had stood for 94 years.



But Calvert-Lewin was kept out by a brilliant Walter Benitez save as the Eagles kept a much-needed first clean sheet in the league since April to take them a point clear of the bottom three in 15th spot.

It could have been three for Pierre Sage’s men had Tyrick Mitchell’s 53rd-minute effort not been ruled out for a tight offside call in the build-up.



Leeds remain unbeaten, but are fifth after missing the chance to go third.

All eyes were on Calvert-Lewin following a dream week.



Recalled by England for the Uefa Nations League games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia after missing out on the World Cup, he had his sights on a Leeds landmark.

Having matched Australian Mark Viduka’s run of scoring in five straight home Prem games 23 years ago, the 29-year-old wanted the joy of six.

Back in 1932, Arthur Hydes was the last Englishman to net in six successive top-flight matches at Elland Road.

But in a sluggish start by the hosts, Calvert-Lewin barely got a sniff against a side that had been desperate in defence this term.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Palace had conceded two or more goals in each of their last 10 Prem matches – second only to Fulham’s run of 13 in 2019.

But they showed some grit in Yorkshire as Daniel Farke’s men were held to a goalless draw for the first time since March.

Argentine keeper Benitez, again deputising for the injured Dean Henderson, was punished for taking too long with his goal-kick and fortunate Tarik Muharemovic steered his header wide from the resulting corner awarded to Leeds.

But Palace calmed down and took control with a couple of counter-attacks at the other end that almost paid off.

Quinten Timber sent a wild finish over after the first in the sixth minute, before the Dutchman slipped through a pass for Jurgen Strand Larsen in the box, but Muharemovic made a timely sliding challenge to deny him a clear sight of goal.



Nico Elvedi did the same as Leeds diced with danger at the back and keeper James Trafford was eventually forced into a low save to stop a low Daichi Kamada strike.

A series of crucial blocks again thwarted Palace before Noah Okafor finally provided an attacking outlet for the hosts when he raced down the left but his low fizzing cross was cut out.

Having fired an earlier effort wide, Ao Tanaka slashed another opportunity off target after Benitez had punched a clearance into his path and left his goal gaping.

Palace, though, punctured the mood of the home crowd with a storming start to the second half where they created three chances to open the scoring.

Yeremy Pino powered in a free-kick from the edge of the box that was pushed away superbly to his right by Trafford, while Jefferson Lerma hooked the resulting corner over from close range.



Kamada lashed a low drive wide before Palace did put the ball in the net when Mitchell arrived late to crash home after Anan Khalaili’s cross had dropped to him.

But on his top-flight debut, referee Adam Herczeg ruled out the strike after Khalaili was adjudged to be offside by VAR when running on to a Pino through-ball.

Relieved, Leeds responded with a first big chance of their own in the 56th minute when James Justin’s right-wing cross was met by the lurking Calvert-Lewin, but his finish was brilliantly blocked by Benitez.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A tense finale followed and Ethan Ampadu had to make an inch-perfect tackle to stop Kamada in the box.

The Japan midfielder then headed agonisingly wide before Muharemovic made a decisive last-ditch challenge to nick the ball away from Ismaila Sarr as he was about to shoot after being teed up by fellow sub Eddie Nketiah.

Atletico star Romero was late to the challenge as Bellingham went to ground and cleared the ball, before they clattered into each other.



Referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias initially deemed the Real star to have been at fault, handing Bellingham a yellow card.

He was quickly swarmed by players pleading their case, with each side blaming the nasty collision on the other.

And VAR also had its reservations, spotting the grisly contact between Romero’s studs and his opponent’s lower leg.

The official was sent to the pitch-side monitor to review the clash, with many fans expecting the former Tottenham defender to see red.

But Arias decided that a yellow card would be punishment enough, while rescinding the caution he had previously shown Bellingham.

It was far from the first yellow shown in the opening half, with that honour going to Atletico boss Diego Simeone.

His first derby since his summer switch was always going to be a risky one for the star.

The referee did end up having to reach for his red card early in the second half, but not for Romero.

Sports.title: Man City 5 Sunderland 3: Erling Haaland sets unique record as Maresca’s men go three points clear after thriller
Sports.content:
Next

ERLING HAALAND had the last word as Manchester City went three points clear at the top on an afternoon of high drama.

But spare a thought for Sunderland forward Brian Brobbey who scored at hat-trick but ended up on the losing side.



You have to go back 19 years for the last time that happened in the Prem – when Roque Santa Cruz did it for Blackburn just down the road from here at Wigan.

The match ball might not be much of a consolation for the Dutchman.



Enzo Maresca had predicted it would be his team’s hardest game of the season and they were given an almighty scare by Sunderland.

On three occasions his team scored only for the Black Cats to hit back within a matter on minutes.

And it was only when Haaland slotted in his 10th goal of the season eight minutes from time that the home crowd could finally breathe easily.

It makes it seven wins out of seven for new boss Maresca – yet that doesn’t begin to tell the story.

City took the lead inside 10 minutes and it was brilliant thinking by City’s Enzo Fernandez.

The record-signing’s free-kick from the right hand side of the box took Robin Roefs by surprise but there was no doubting the quality of it.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

This was the Argentine’s first goal since he equalised for his country against England in the World Cup semi-final just over two months ago.

And the Sunderland fans who booed his name before kick off would have hated it.

But within three minutes it was all forgotten as another Enzo- Le Fee this time – threaded a beaut of a pass to Brian Brobbey who finished clinically.

It had been a breathless start but it was just getting going.



Just before the half hour City edged back in front – as Josko Gvardiol and Erling Haaland were both involved before Antoine Semenyo moved it on to Cherki.

It was a scruffy build up in many ways but there was no doubting the brilliance of the finish as the French maestro shifted it onto his right foot and drilled a low shot past Roefs.

This time the lead lasted slightly longer – four minutes to be exact.

Just like last week, City were involved in a lengthy VAR check and this time it went against them.



At Old Trafford Enzo Maresca’s men got a huge slice of fortune from the video assistants as Erling Haaland’s winner was allowed to stand.

Here there was a long wait while Brobbey’s second equaliser of the afternoon was checked.

Thomas Meunier was very close to being off as he was picked out by another super pass from Enzo Le Fee.

The Belgian international squared for Brobbey to tap into an empty net. It was extremely tight but VAR Michael Salisbury gave it the green light.



Yet there was still bags more drama to come before half time though as Marc Guehi challenged Dan Ballard tor a cross from the right.

It dropped kindly for Semenyo who thumped a low shot through the crowd to restore his team’s lead.

Before half-time, Haaland somehow missed a chance served upto him on a plate by new boy Iliman Ndiaye – firing it wide with the goal at his mercy.

And at the other end Gianluigi Donnarumma had to make an acrobatic save to keep out a deflected shot by Brobbey.



It couldn’t carry on like this, could it?

Well yes actually.

City fans probably thought they could finally breathe easily as Kevin Danso and Nordi Mukiele got in each other’s way and Semenyo thumped home the loose ball.

But just two minutes later Brobbey completed his hat-trick as Granit Xhaka’s pass was squared by Nilson Angulo – and the forward had the easiest job to finish it off.



That made it seven goals in the first hour – and the points were still anyone’s.

The visitors could have been level minutes later as Ballard’s header was almost put into his own net by City skipper Ruben Dias.

The Portuguese defender managed to get back to acrobatically clear off his own line and City’s lead remained intact – just.

An equaliser would not have flattered the visitors but as is often the case here, the big guy had the final word.



Sunderland were the only Prem team Haaland had not scored against and that record looked likely to remain intact.

However Prem defenders know you can’t keep him quiet for long and there he was eight minutes from time finishing off a cross by Josko Gvardiol.

Just like in last weekend’s derby it was initially flagged offside due to the Croatian defender going too early.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the VAR showed he had timed his run to perfection and Haaland was able to embark on a belated celebration once more.



And that was that for what was surely the game of the season so far.

Sports.title: Palace secure valuable point at unbeaten Leeds
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace secured a useful point at in-form and unbeaten Leeds as Pierre Sage's side produced a much-improved defensive display to hold the hosts to a goalless draw at Elland Road.

The stalemate was enough to lift Sage's side one point clear of the relegation zone heading into the three-week international break.

Palace arrived having conceded 11 goals in their opening four Premier League games but, after a cagey first half, grew into the contest and were the more threatening side after the break. Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net only for it to be ruled out for offside.

Leeds, unbeaten coming into the game after an impressive 4-1 win over Newcastle, struggled to reproduce that attacking fluency. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who had scored in each of his previous five Premier League home games, was largely starved of service, eventually being denied by Walter Benitez after the break.

Palace had chances to snatch it late on, with Adam Wharton continuing to influence proceedings and Eddie Nketiah and Ismaila Sarr combining for an opening that Tarik Muharemovic brilliantly recovered to stop. Leeds threw on attacking reinforcements and switched shape, but could not find the breakthrough.

For Palace, after conceding two or more goals in each of their previous 10 Premier League matches, they finally kept a clean sheet - and did so against a Leeds side that had scored 12 goals across their previous five home league games. The performance gives Sage a platform to build on after a difficult opening month.

The key moments from Elland Road

10: SMART TACKLE! Muharemovic makes a crucial intervention to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen after Quinten Timber had slipped the Palace striker through on goal.

22: OVER! Ao Tanaka fires over from close range after Leeds' long throw caused problems in the Palace box.

31: PALACE PUSHING! Strand Larsen, Timber and Wharton all see efforts blocked as Palace threaten to break the deadlock.

53: OFFSIDE, NO GOAL! Mitchell fires Palace in front after Anan Khalaili's cross, but VAR confirms Khalaili was offside in the build-up.

57: WHAT A SAVE! Benitez produces an excellent reaction stop to deny Calvert-Lewin after James Justin's cross picked out the in-form striker.

71: PENALTY APPEAL! Daichi Kamada goes down under pressure from Ethan Ampadu, but the referee waves away Palace's claims.

83: BIG CHANCE! Wharton's clever ball releases Sarr into the area, but Justin recovers brilliantly to deny the Palace substitute.

88: PALACE OPPORTUNITY! Nketiah breaks clear after being played in by Wharton but chooses to square for Sarr, allowing Muharemovic to make a crucial recovery.

Palace showed exactly what they had been missing

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They leave with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

Leeds were strangely flat. Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Benitez was there to deny him.

In the end, 0-0 feels like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

For Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround.

Farke: It was important to extend the unbeaten run

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking to Sky Sports:



"You're always just 100 per cent happy once you win the game, and of course, we wanted after our nearly perfect start to win this home game. Football-wise, it was not our best performance, but we also played against a well structured side.

"I think we were a bit too loose with the ball today, and in the execution in the opponent's half, in the final third.

"Our defending behaviour for 60 minutes was excellent. We took more risks and it was a more open game, a bit like a basketball game in the end.

"It also felt that they could perhaps win it in the end. It was one of those days when you don't have your best performance-wise, but then you have to dig in and fight.

"It was also important to keep the clean sheet and extend the unbeaten run, and for that we take this point."

Sage: Palace deserved more than a point

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage speaking to Sky Sports:

"We worked a lot during the last week on this, and we tested on our game on Thursday, but I think it was better and better. We conceded less chances than before. We conceded a big one, and our keeper made a big save. So I have to congratulate Walter Benitez for that.

"But at the end, during the game, not only the defensive part, but I think we deserve better."

On whether Palace deserved to win:

"Yes, I think because we create some chances and without scoring, the one that was cancelled by the VAR is normal because there's an offside. But it's a little bit frustrating because I think the players gave a lot in this game, and at the end they deserve something else than a draw."

On the fine margins:

"Yes, and I think we will speak about that in the future because one time is good, but we have to do it more."

Robinson: Neither side lost points - both gained one

Paul Robinson on Sky Sports:

"I thought Palace were excellent after the break.

"Both goalkeepers had to make excellent saves, but we were limited to few goalscoring chances. We witnessed two sides cancelling each other out.

"Neither side has lost points, but have gained one."

Sports.title: Littler's bid for major clean sweep ended by crushing Clayton defeat
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 is over after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Littler was hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic monopoly over the year - but ran into an inspired Clayton.

Clayton will take on fellow Welshman Gerwyn Price in Sunday's second semi-final, after England's Ross Smith meets home favourite Gian van Veen in the first semi-final, with the final to follow.

What next for Littler?

Littler can still sweep the ranking events - the World Series Finals, like the World Cup and Premier League, is non-ranked - if he wins the remaining four majors in Leicester, Dortmund, Wolverhampton and Minehead this autumn.

'The Nuke' has work to do to reach the Players Championship Finals, though, as he sits 125th on the Order of Merit in that series with six events of the regular season remaining and only the top 64 players advance to the finale in Somerset from November 27-29.

"It's the pressure. Everyone talks about: 'Can he do the whole year and win all the big majors.' It gives big pressure. He wants to perform.

"He's the best player at the moment, but everyone is fallible. Everyone wants your scalp, and Jonny Clayton did it perfectly.

"In all honestly, Littler missed some crucial shots.

Image: Littler's performance was purely down to 'pressure', according to Raymond van Barneveld

Littler latest big name to exit in Amsterdam

Victory at the World Series of Darts Finals would have been Littler's second in three years, having beaten Michael Smith to triumph in 2024 before losing to Michael van Gerwen in the final 12 months ago.

Littler had suffered scares earlier this week, rallying from 3-1 down to defeat Danny Noppert 6-4 in round one and then surviving a last-leg shoot-out versus Nathan Aspinall to win 10-9 in the last 16.

World No 2 Luke Humphries was eliminated by Dirk van Duijvenbode in round two on Saturday, while defending champion Van Gerwen fell in the opening round on Thursday, losing to Daryl Gurney.

Image: Luke Humphries was knocked out by Dirk van Duijvenbode in round two

Van Gerwen's World Series Finals victory last season is the only major he has won since 2023 and he has failed to reach an individual quarter-final in this year's majors.

The 37-year-old did make it to the final of the World Cup of Darts for Netherlands alongside doubles partner Van Veen, where the Dutch duo were beaten by England's Littler and Humphries.

That World Cup victory for Littler in Frankfurt in June means the European Championship is the only major title absent from his CV - something he will hope to rectify in Dortmund later this year.

Sports.title: Eight goals and complete CHAOS as Man City somehow beat Sunderland
Sports.content:
Manchester City head into the extended international break three points clear at the top of the Premier League after edging a completely bonkers, gloriously chaotic eight-goal thriller against Sunderland, winning 5-3.

Enzo Maresca's side knew that any positive result would see them open up a gap on nearest rivals Arsenal after Mikel Arteta's side slumped to defeat at Brighton on Saturday. But Maresca surely did not plan to do it in the chaotic manner that transpired, with City trading blows with Sunderland as though it were a training match.

Enzo Fernandez's clever free-kick put City ahead inside nine minutes, but that was merely the beginning of the pandemonium. Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo also found the net in a first half that produced five goals, with Sunderland's undefendable striker Brian Brobbey grabbing two.

Man City led three times in first half Man City led 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2 in the first half, making it only the seventh match in Premier League history to see a team take the lead on three separate occasions in the first half alone.

City's performance was littered with mistakes, particularly defensively, as Brobbey bullied Ruben Dias and completed a remarkable 33-minute hat-trick after Semenyo had netted his second of the afternoon to make it 4-2 in favour of the hosts.

Image: Erling Haaland has now scored against every Premier League opponent he has faced

Erling Haaland had the final say, breaking his Sunderland duck to complete the Premier League set, having now found the net all 25 opponents he has faced in the English top flight. Just another astonishing subplot from a ridiculous afternoon.

As a whole, the game could not have been further removed from the picture of control so often associated with Pep Guardiola's City. Out of possession, Maresca's blueprint left them alarmingly open, with Sunderland needing little invitation to exploit the gaps. Brobbey accumulated a personal expected goals value greater than every Premier League team this weekend, bar his own.

Brilliant Brobbey Brian Brobbey is the sixth instance of a player scoring a Premier League hat-trick but ending the match on the losing side, and the first since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn in 2007.

Sunderland might have left the Etihad empty handed but do so with plenty of credit after an attacking display that arguably outshone City's, registering nine shots on target. City's players sank to their knees at the final whistle, a clear indication of just how close they came to letting victory slip in the to and fro of such an intense battle.

"I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3," Maresca concluded with a smile. "But I knew how difficult it would be."

Regis Le Bris: Belief remains high despite punishing loss

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris:

"We didn't compromise our identity. We're really proud to play our football and we went toe-to-toe with one of the best sides in Europe.

"We created many chances and every small mistake gets punished at that level. This is the reality of the Premier League and we're here to learn.

"The team is really resilient and the belief is high about our qualities, the way we can hurt the opponent. It's not a surprise, but we are frustrated because we came here with the belief it was possible to win."

On Brobbey's hat-trick: "It's positive because it's impossible to tell the story differently, but it's clear for us that he's a good striker, he's getting better with every game, and his mentality is superb. It was just a question of time."

Sports.title: Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship, McIlroy falters despite late surge
Sports.content:
JJ Spaun surged through a packed leaderboard on Sunday afternoon at the BMW PGA Championship to win his second DP World Tour event and his first outside of a major championship.

An utterly thrilling final round of golf unfolded at Wentworth, with multiple players, including Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Manuel Elvira, all racing to the finish line, but all struggled to pull away with the lead.

There was heartbreak for Elvira, who had the chance to leapfrog Spaun at the top of the leaderboard after tying the 2025 US Open champion with an eagle on the 17th hole.

With Spaun already in the clubhouse at 17 under, the Spaniard needed a birdie on the 18th to win his first-ever DP World Tour title, but he came unstuck, finding a fairway bunker with his tee shot before sending his bunker shot well past the green.

He attempted to chip back on but agonisingly sent his shot into the bunker before ultimately confirming Spaun's two-stroke win with a double bogey.

Spaun, who was omitted from Brandt Snedeker's USA President's Cup Team, was out to prove a point this week in Surrey, and the 2025 US Open champion showcased his composure to rally from an early bogey with six birdies to post a final round score of 67, and seal victory with a score of 17 under.

Elvira would tie McIlroy, Rai, and Adam Scott at 15 under par for second place.

More to follow…

What's next?

The next DP World Tour event is the FedEx Open de France, held at Le Golf National - the venue for Europe's 2018 Ryder Cup win - and beginning Thursday.

Team USA chase a record-extending 11th consecutive victory over the International Team at the Presidents Cup, held at Medinah Country Club in Illinois and also starting Thursday.

Sports.title: Bolton prevail at Norwich in seven-goal thriller
Sports.content:
Norwich suffered their second successive 4-3 Sky Bet Championship defeat as Bolton came out on top in a thrilling encounter at Carrow Road.

The Canaries, who lost by the same scoreline at Middlesbrough last Saturday, again traded goals with their opponents at a rapid rate before Trotters substitute Atsuki Ito had the final say midway through the second period.

A breathless first half saw Norwich pegged back twice after taking the lead through their first attack of the game in the fifth minute.

Andre Brooks slipped in Mo Toure through the inside-right channel and the in-form Australian striker fired home in spectacular fashion from just outside the area, his first-time effort flying past Gavin Bazunu before the goalkeeper had had a chance to react.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Atsuki Ito makes it 4-3 to Bolton vs Norwich during their chaotic Championship clash

Bolton were level within three minutes, however, through another well-taken goal, Thierry Gale cutting inside from the left before beating Vladan Kovacevic at his near post with a precise finish.

Toure then had another effort ruled out by a clear-cut offside decision before his afternoon was cut short after just a quarter of an hour when he injured his arm after falling awkwardly.

Norwich regained their lead in the 19th minute as a deep corner from Oscar Schwartau was headed home off the upright by centre-half Ruairi McConville for his first goal in Norwich colours.

The Trotters continued to look a threat going forward, with a couple of decent chances going begging before they levelled again in the 42nd minute.

After the Canaries had made a hash of playing out from the back, Max Conway was able to play in a low cross that eventually fell for Gaizka Larrazabal, who unleashed a perfectly-struck half-volley which flew into the net from some 20 yards out.

Image: Gaizka Larrazabal celebrates after equalising for Bolton at Carrow Road

Bolton stunned the home faithful by going ahead for the first time less than two minutes after the interval. A neat attack down the right ended with Kyliane Dong playing in Sam Dalby who produced a neat chipped finish to beat Kovacevic.

There was no letting up with the entertainment, with Norwich getting back on level terms in the 61st minute. Substitute Paris Maghoma made an immediate impact by sweeping the ball wide to the fast-breaking Jack Stacey, who burst into the area before firing home off the far post.

Kovacevic made a good reaction stop to prevent Larrazabal from quickly restoring Bolton's lead but they did not have to wait long for their fourth of the afternoon.

With 72 minutes on the clock, substitute Ito, who had only just been introduced, wriggled his way through the centre of the home defence before calmly finding the bottom corner.

The managers

Norwich's Philippe Clement:

"There were some good moments for us out there today but obviously everything is overshadowed by conceding four goals.

"It was a frantic game - and you don't win many games of football if you concede four.

"I thought we started well and scored a good goal but then we conceded a goal that was too easy. Their winger was surrounded by four of our players but still managed to get his shot away and hit the net.

"Their second equaliser was a result of an attacking player only thinking about attacking, not defending, and then we fall apart as a team.

"There were some hard lessons to be learned but I believe what these guys can do together and we need to reset and make sure these sort of things don't happen again."

Bolton's Steven Schumacher:

"Every game is going to be difficult for us at this level because of what we are up against and this is an especially tough place to come.

"It was a great game for the neutral, as I thought it would be, with lots of chances created and obviously we are delighted to come away with the three points.

"I was really impressed with the character we showed to get back in the game after twice going behind - and then didn't let it affect us when they got it back to 3-3.

"We got in front again and then had the energy and resilience to see out the game.

"We have played well in our other away games this season without getting a reward so I am glad we have finally got something for our efforts.

"I am especially pleased for our fans. Nearly 1,000 came down for a Sunday lunchtime kick-off and gave us terrific support and it's obviously nice for them too."

Sports.title: Isak wins it for Liverpool on Iraola's return to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak scored the winning goal as Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0 on Andoni Iraola's return to the Vitality Stadium.

A tense game was settled just after the hour mark as Isak latched onto Cody Gakpo's cross - via a slight nick off Florian Wirtz.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool won at Bournemouth thanks to this goal from Alexander Isak

Liverpool snatched victory on a day where they struggled in large parts, with Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher criticising their first-half display, as the Cherries dominated. "Iraola probably cannot believe how lethargic Liverpool look," he said on co-commentary duty.

But Bournemouth lacked the clinical touch as they remain winless under Marco Rose in the league. Their best chance fell to Evanilson, whose near-post flick from Marcus Tavernier's cross was kept out brilliantly by Alisson - who palmed out the effort from behind him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool stopper Alisson reacts quickly as James Tavernier fires the ball across the face of goal and Evanilson meets it with a neat flick.

The victory is Liverpool's second in the league this season as they go into the international break in sixth place. Bournemouth, meanwhile, sit level on points with Coventry in 17th place.

Alexander the great(er)! In five games (4 goals) this season, Alexander Isak has already surpassed his Premier League goal tally for the entirety of last season in the competition (3 goals in 14 apps).

The key moments from the south coast

18: HUGE SAVE! Tavernier's cross from the right is flicked towards the near post by Evanilson but Alisson makes a huge stop.

34: SAVE! Bradley Barcola cuts inside from the left wing and his effort is saved by Djordje Petrovic.

36: JUST WIDE! Dominik Szoboszlai hits a trademark free-kick which bounces just the wrong side of the post.

61: GOAL! Isak crashes Liverpool in front after Gakpo did well down the right wing.

68: SAVE! Bournemouth look for a response but Evanilson can only curl into Alisson's clutches.

70: BIG BLOCK! Gakpo pokes Isak through on goal but James Hill comes across for a big block.

90+2: BIG CHANCE! Lewis Koumas has the chance to seal it for Liverpool but his curling effort inside the box from Victor Munoz's pass is straight at Petrovic.

Iraola unhappy with how Liverpool started game

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola to Sky Sports:

"I'm obviously happy with the result. I know it's a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. We could see in the game, at the beginning in the first 20 minutes, we weren't at the level at the game, and it has cost us until afterwards, where we finished the first half better.

"The second half we played better. But that beginning of the game kind of - not surprised us because we knew where we were coming to - but it was difficult for us.

"We could see a bit later when Bournemouth started to get tired that in the second half we controlled the game much better. We even had chances to finish but didn't score the second one.

"But that first part of the game, we were not winning duels, second balls and when they play with this intensity, you have to be at their level."

Analysis: Where would Liverpool be without Cody Gakpo?

Image: Isak celebrates with Cody Gakpo

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

In every single Liverpool game he's started this season, Cody Gakpo has produced a golden moment in front of goal.

A goal at Newcastle on the opening weekend, a silky against Nottingham Forest, assists for both goals in the win over Ipswich, another assist and a goal against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup - but this intervention at Bournemouth was the best of the lot.

With Liverpool struggling for attacking influence, Gakpo's hard-fought run and cross down the right wing was vital in the build-up to Alexader Isak's winner. "The difficult part of the goal is from him," said Iraola about Gakpo, who is unfortunate not to be accredited with the assist.

But Gakpo also starred defensively at Bournemouth, winning more duels than any other player on the pitch. He shut down one of the Cherries' biggest threats. "I know Adrien Truffert very well and he demands a lot from you defensively. Cody today has been very important in both ways."

Looking at this form, it is absolutely staggering that Liverpool considered sanctioning the sale of Gakpo this summer. Where would they be without him?

Rose: Bournemouth panicked in tight situations

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose to Sky Sports:

"We couldn't see that one team deserved to win. We played really good in the first 25 minutes and then it got more open.

"We had to work really hard to get chances but we conceded an easy goal.

"In both boxes, you had to be ready and be present. In the end, they scored the goal with one situation and we put a lot of effort into creating chances.

"We panicked a little bit in tight situations. We were fit and I thought we could bring more energy into the game. It is disappointing.

"It was an opportunity to win, right now we have three points from five games and it is disappointing, I think we missed details."

Sports.title: DP World Tour plans to keep Play-Offs in UAE despite player safety concerns
Sports.content:
DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.

The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.

Image: Fitzpatrick is defending champion at the DP World Tour Championship

"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports. "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

"Work has started and we're building stuff at Yas Links and at the Jumeirah Golf Estates, so our intention is to go ahead.

"We clearly need to keep in touch with travel advisors and other people who help with us, but our plan is definitely to play the Play-Offs in the UAE."

Defending DP World Tour champion Fitzpatrick said on Wednesday that he was "not that comfortable" playing in Dubai, given its proximity to the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, although McIlroy was less concerned.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of day four from the 2025 DP World Championship in Dubai, where Fitzpatrick edged out Rory McIlroy in a dramatic finish

"If the local governments feel like it's safe to put on these events, they are not going to put their citizens or people visiting in harm's way," McIlroy said after his opening round at the BMW PGA Championship.

"I love the Middle East. I have a lot of friends there and I'm looking forward to going back for sure."

'Future looks bright for DP World Tour'

The DP World Tour announced its 2027 schedule at the BMW PGA Championship, with the Flagship Event being held a week later next year and immediately after the centenary Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.

"I think the way the schedule's set up, with golf in America stopping at the end of August, we've got the opportunity to shine from September 1 until the end of January. I think that'll mean more of the guys will come and play in great events like this and some of the other tournaments as well."

Kinnings added: "I have to say, I couldn't be more excited. I think it's a huge opportunity for international golf. We clearly have wonderful players and we have an opportunity to shine in the schedule."

The DP World Tour has yet to announce whether it will impose sanctions for its members wishing to play in the new iteration of the LIV Golf League, should LIV 2.0 go ahead as planned in 2027, with Kinnings keen to see the strongest fields possible on his circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy feels it is inevitable some players will choose to leave LIV Golf and believes the DP World Tour can benefit

"We've been very consistent on the whole question and we're going to continue that way," Kinnings insisted. "What will happen with LIV is entirely speculation, but from our perspective we want to find a balance. As a business, we just love to have the best fields we possibly can with the best players.

"But we're also a member's organisation and our job is purely to make sure we look out for the best interests of the members. We have a wonderful tour, amazing culture and that's because of the players, so nothing's going to change on that front.

"I think we're in a stronger position as we can possibly be. We've got great partners and the future looks bright - we now just need to work out exactly what it looks like."

Sports.title: Semenyo helps chaotic Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 after Brobbey hat-trick
Sports.content:
Manchester City sent a message to Arsenal with this chaotic victory that takes Enzo Maresca’s team three points clear as leaders for the three-week international break.

Until the Premier League resumes on 10 October City can enjoy their view from the top while Mikel Arteta’s champions have to stew following Saturday’s 3-0 humbling at Brighton.

Yet Maresca will review this game because City lacked control and may not have enjoyed a 5-3 win that featured two Antoine Semenyo strikes for them, a Brian Brobbey hat-trick for Sunderland, with Enzo Fernández, Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland the other scorers.

Maresca’s side are entertaining for the neutral and heart-palpitating for the manager. When the normally calm Rúben Dias hit the ball towards his goal and scrambled to hoof off the line, this was City in microcosm, versus Régis Le Bris’ potent visitors. The conclusion, though, from the season opening phase is that City will compete with the Gunners to the end of the title race - providing they become less fragile.

Sunderland conceded first by allowing a break at corner that ended in Dayann Methalie chopping down Iliman Ndiaye. Next came a moment of high Fernández skill from a free-kick along the right-hand edge of the box. City’s No 17 asked Ndiaye to alter position in the area, then guided the ball straight home, on the near side, his instruction to the winger hoodwinking Robin Roefs, Sunderland’s No 1, who ended up on his backside.

It was a first goal for Fernández goal since his equaliser in the World Cup semi-final for Argentina against England and was an excellent moment for City, only for them to fall asleep seconds later.

View image in fullscreen Brian Brobbey gets to take the match ball home but the Sunderland striker looks dejected after the defeat at Manchester City Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock

Enzo Le Fée is one of Sunderland’s star acts and the pinpoint pass into Brobbey that split Dias and Matheus Nunes showed why. The No 9’s first touch was smart, allowing him to then beat, with the outside of his right boot, the onrushing Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Maresca had billed the contest as City’s toughest so far and you saw now that this was not regulation respectful manager-speak. Le Bris’ side pinged the ball about and were quick to fire it into the danger area. Yet, when feeling too comfortable while playing out from the back, City pounced again.

Kevin Danso’s loose pass from his area was nabbed by Ndiaye and the ball went instantly to Haaland near the penalty spot. Semenyo took over, tapped to Cherki and the Frenchman made space and threaded in.

That made it 2-1 to City with half an hour gone. Three minutes later a breathless opening period had another twist. Le Fée slipped in Thomas Meunier, the wide right forward crossed, and Brobbey could not miss. Following a prolonged video assistant referee check Sunderland’s second stood: Brobbey and Meunier being offside was the question and it appeared marginal.

Again, Maresca’s side suffered due to naivety. And, again, they roved upfield and breached their visitors’ rearguard. This time Cherki hit Marc Guéhi with a chip from the right that provoked a scramble in Sunderland’s area. The ball came out to Semenyo who powered in to restore City’s lead.

By the interval it should have been 4-2 but the normally lethal Haaland splayed wide after Ndiaye teed him up. The last bit of action had a mis-hit Brobbey effort nearly chipping Donnarumma who needed his 6ft 5in to tip over.

Maresca surely wanted the match slowed down in the second half, with the ball at City feet. Yet still holes were punched in them as when Elliot Anderson was caught upfield and Noah Sadiki ran into space and ballooned over.

Another goal looked to be needed because Sunderland were relentless. Cherki’s curving pass right to Ndiaye created a chance for the fourth but the winger’s touch was clumsy. Better was Semenyo’s decisiveness that made it 4-2. Cherki’s pass caused Mukiele a problem, the ball went to City’s Frenchman, and he arrowed into the far right corner.

Could City breathe? No was the answer. Anderson may have been lucky not to concede a penalty when the ball struck a hand in the area - another indication of City’s scruffiness, and then Brobbey’s third came. Granit Xhaka delivered from the right, Angulo helped the ball on, and the Dutchman converted.

This was seven goals before the hour mark in what was a basketball-like affair packed with incident that, next, included Haaland’s late fifth.

Jérémy Doku, on for Ndiaye, had Josko Gvardiol slaloming along the left, the defender’s cross to the far post slid beyond Roefs by the Norwegian. Initially flagged as offside the VAR overturned the linesman’s call and that was 5-3 – the end of the scoring on an afternoon that will not be forgotten soon.

Sports.title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
At the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights at Bournemouth last season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola hopes they become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish. Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in the Premier League.

In midweek, Iraola was rooting for his former club on their European bow but promised a businesslike return to Bournemouth and stepped off one of the two Liverpool team coaches with a game face. Tommy Elphick, who captained Bournemouth to the Premier League in 2015 and followed Iraola to Liverpool, embraced old colleagues on the pitch side before the warm up and Dominik Szoboszlai and Milos Kerkez shared an embrace with Alex Toth, their Hungary teammate. Kerkez replaced Kostas Tsimikas at left-back in one of three changes from their stalemate with Fulham.

It was fitting that the bass of Never Tear Us Apart sounded over the speakers as Iraola walked along the front row of the home dugout, shaking hands with his successor Marco Rose’s staff. Iraola’s body of work, improving season on season and eclipsing Bournemouth’s points record in successive campaigns led him to this point. The transition was so smooth Rose and Iraola spent an hour together on Iraola’s last day at Bournemouth’s training base, only stopping because Tiago Pinto, Bournemouth’s sporting director, interrupted to remind them there were other things on the agenda.

All the niceties, Iraola said, could wait until afterwards. Pablo de la Torre, his fitness coach who was part of his staff at Bournemouth, made that clear within the opening 30 seconds, wresting the ball away from Adam Smith to delay the hosts taking a quick throw-in. Bournemouth were intent on building on Thursday’s history-making victory in the Basque Country and had the best chance of the first half. Iraola marched from the away technical area back towards the dugout after Alisson’s smart right-hand save prevented Evanilson’s front-post flick from squeezing in at his near post.

Szoboszlai dropped a typically vicious free-kick wide of Djordje Petrovic’s post and Petrovic saved a deflected Bradley Barcola shot with his legs, but Liverpool spent much of the first half containing Bournemouth’s threats; they attacked from all angles, as Iraola knew they would.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola applauds the fans after victory at the Vitality Stadium. Photograph: Ian Walton/AP

Early in the second half, Szoboszlai was booked for a foul on Alex Scott but Liverpool showed glimpses of their quality. “Yes, yes,” Iraola said, encouraging Isak as the Sweden striker made tracks down the right flank, only for his cross to end up with the ball flying towards the scaffolding structure in a corner of the ground, part of Bournemouth’s ongoing stadium upgrade. Florian Wirtz saw a disguised pass for Isak cut out and Bournemouth flew forward, the again-impressive Jérémy Jacquet making it difficult for Ryan Christie to connect with a low cross at the front post. Christie chopped inside Szoboszlai close to the touchline and then Scott switched play with a pinged diagonal pass.
