Bournemouth seemed to be growing in confidence but then Gakpo easily bypassed Adrien Truffert, usually such a dependable performer since signing from Rennes last summer. Gakpo crossed from the right and while James Hill dived in to extinguish the threat of Wirtz at the front post, the ball dropped to an unmarked Isak on the edge of the six-yard box to stroke the ball in. From there Bournemouth seemed to run out of juice and Liverpool eked out victory. Iraola pointed his players towards the scoreboard after they won a free-kick on halfway and, seconds later, it was job done.

Sports.title: Leeds extend unbeaten start to season after stalemate with Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Perhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing with Crystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s side enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself.

Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts suffered their first blank.

A victory by two clear goals would have meant a best-ever start to a Premier League campaign for Leeds but they were blunt in the final third. There was even a level of discontent amid a ponderous performance with fans chanting “forward” as they failed to replicate the thrashing of Newcastle on Monday.

“Mixed emotions,” Farke said. “We would have preferred to win, but the reality is it is 38 game days. It is not always magic nights under the floodlights, champagne football, you overrun the opponent and score goals for fun. Sometimes it is a scruffy Sunday afternoon when you have to dig in. This was one of these games.”

Farke is into the final year of his contract and signing a new one is a priority for him and the club. His stature has grown over the past 10 months, with Leeds the fifth-best performing team in the division since December 2025 and the German will likely be rewarded for bringing stability to the club in the coming weeks as Leeds aim to build on strong foundations.

The most notable moment of the opening quarter came when Walter Benítez took too long to distribute the ball. The referee, Adam Herczeg, making his Premier League debut and fully aware of the rules, awarded Leeds a corner as punishment. It was a tentative game in the autumn sunshine, lacking intensity and quality, with Ao Tanaka snatching at a shot the closest anyone got to threatening a goal.

Around the half-hour mark something akin to a football match broke out as nervousness was replaced by urgency. Jørgen Strand Larsen and Quinten Timber engineered a chance for Palace which was blocked and allowed Leeds to break through Noah Okafor down the left, although his cross was turned behind.

Palace had the greater quality, with Adam Wharton and Timber comfortable in possession in the middle of the park, while Yéremy Pino whizzed around in the hope of finding an opener. It was controlled play, as the visitors took their time in the buildup, although there was often very little at the end of it as James Trafford was left unthreatened.

Leeds on the other hand would burst into life for brief moments as the full-backs flew forward, changing the dynamic in an instant but Palace’s centre-backs and wing-backs were built to deal with these rapid transitions, leaving Dominic Calvert-Lewin starved of service. Benítez could relax and re-read the laws of the game, having failed to face a single shot on target in the opening 40 minutes.

View image in fullscreen James Justin stretches to block an effort from Eddie Nketiah. Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock

Palace pushed the fast forward button at the break and Mitchell put the ball in the back of the net from a fine move down the right. The glory turned to anguish when the video assistant referee (VAR) intervened to show Anan Khalaili was offside in the buildup, causing an eruption inside Elland Road.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Leeds were sluggish but the warning from Mitchell caused a reaction and they were almost ahead when Calvert-Lewin’s only real chance was saved by Benítez. The England striker was given too much space to get on the end of a cross but his sidefooted volley was weak.

There was a touch of menace in the game as Tanaka and Wharton were booked in quick succession, the first for a cynical foul and the latter after lunging in late without a hope of winning the ball, ensuring Herczeg was far busier than the two goalkeepers.

Leeds were completely ineffective in open play, Ethan Ampadu engaged in a long-throwathon. Every few minutes he would trot to one sideline or the other to pick up the ball and hurl it into the box but Palace were alive to the danger. “We had many set-pieces today, but also today we didn’t have the best quality of the delivery,” Farke said.

Palace edged the match and Daichi Kamada could have won it late on but his header drifted inches wide. Sage will be relieved to see his defence so well organised and untroubled after conceding 11 in the first four games, leading to plenty of early scrutiny on his appointment. “Especially when I read the social media, there’s a big pressure.” Sage said. “But you know, I don’t care about that. I do my job with honesty, I give my best with my skills and my limits. And in the end, I have no regrets with what I do.”

Sports.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
Sports.content:
If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.

That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.

It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.

But nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over their rivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.

The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.

“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.

View image in fullscreen Tempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”

What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust the Celtic board – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?

Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.

Quick Guide Roundup: Vrancken bewildered by VAR as Hearts frustrated at Kilmarnock Show Wouter Vrancken was left bewildered by the “strange” video assistant referee decision to rule out an early Hearts goal in their 1-1 draw at bottom-placed Kilmarnock. The Jambos thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Laurent Mendy’s effort – which appeared to be going wide – was diverted into the net by the Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. But the VAR, Matthew MacDermid, advised Duncan Nicolson to rule it out as the ball had accidentally struck Mendy’s hand. Killie went ahead a few minutes later through a Jamie McCart own goal before Stephen Kingsley equalised in the 86th minute (pictured). But Vrancken cited similarities with the recent incident involving Manchester United’s Harry Maguire against Ipswich and felt Mendy’s inadvertent handball should have been rendered irrelevant by McCarthy heading the ball into the net. “For me, when it’s such a clear situation, it’s strange that the VAR comes in between and rules wrong,” said the Belgian. “We had a meeting last week about the laws of the game and the refs did their explanation but when you don’t see them applied in the game, then I’m thinking this is strange." Martin Boyle ended Hibernian’s losing streak at home after they fought back to claim a point in a 1-1 draw against Aberdeen. The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet. Managerless Hibs – with John Potter in interim charge after David Gray’s midweek sacking – looked bereft of confidence for long spells. However, the Leith side – who had lost six successive games at Easter Road – earned a share of the spoils when Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground. Steven Pressley praised Joe Westley for the bravery he showed by playing in Dundee's 2-1 home win over Motherwell. The former Burnley striker fractured his cheekbone against Hearts a fortnight ago but declared himself available after deciding against having surgery. Instead, he played wearing a protective mask and nett Dundee’s opening goal from the penalty spot before Bradley Fink doubled their advantage. Alex Lowry pulled one back for the visitors just before the break but the home side held on. Pressley said: “Joe showed great courage. But he gave a wonderful performance, without any trepidation. Joe was fearless in everything he did and to score a goal is really important for him because he lives off them." Jim Goodwin hailed his side’s performance as the perfect tonic as Dundee United defeated St Mirren 3-0 in a one-sided contest in Paisley, with first-half goals from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru. It was Goodwin’s first appearance in the dugout since a recent health scare and the United manager said: “On a personal note, it was great to be back. Certainly the best medicine that I could have hoped for was that type of result and performance." A stunning set-piece strike from Enes Alic in the sixth minute of stoppage time secured a dramatic 1-1 draw for 10-man St Johnstone against Falkirk. Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabaté’s 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour. But Alic found the top corner from 25 yards to move Simo Valakari’s side up to sixth place. Press Association Photograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

There was fury here but precious little focus, plenty of passion but no real patterns of play, no order to the chaos, no real idea of how to keep the ball or fashion a chance. Rangers dominated the central areas, where Dan Neil and Nicolas Raskin are already forging a formidable partnership and James Penrice merrily stomped all over the place.

O’Neill gambled on a back five, on Luke McCowan in a sort of withdrawn winger role, discarded both at half-time, rolled through his substitutions, but the plan never really emerged from the fog. Celtic are basically like the tangled ball of printer cables and headphone wires in the bottom drawer, where you’re never quite sure whether you’re unpicking the knots or making them tighter.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Emmanuel Fernandez got a rough ride early on, Tierney clipped the bar from distance and Ivor Pandur made a fine save from Colby Donovan early in the second half. That was basically it, as far as explicit threat went. Donovan’s header was the only Celtic shot on target.

“For a young team, it’s brilliant that they can take the good from this,” said McInnes. “Coming to places like this, it won’t get much more difficult. It’s only three points, but in the context of the season it was important for lots of reasons.” He knows, of course, that Rangers are not the finished article. But right now there is a power vacuum at the top of Scottish football and his improving side may as well be the one to fill it.

Sports.title: Zidane’s next move as France coach may reveal the wizard behind the curtain | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Even in his playing days, Zinedine Zidane seemed unknowable. As a manager, the sense of distance has only grown. He won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid without ever giving a sense of what his idea of football looked like.

France are perhaps the most perplexing football country: a squad that teems with such talent that a B team would be serious contenders at a World Cup, that reached three major finals under Didier Deschamps with a sense of unfulfilment, a team that progressed but rarely entranced, or at least didn’t until this summer’s World Cup, when they attacked with gusto and ended up overrun in midfield by Spain.

On Friday, the two come together as Zidane, for the first time, leads France in their Nations League fixture against Turkey, an enigmatic coach leading a mercurial squad.

Zidane is one of five coaches to have won the Champions League on three or more occasions, ranking alongside Bob Paisley, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique and behind only Carlo Ancelotti. He is the only manager to win three successive Champions Leagues and yet few would consider him one of the game’s elite coaches. In that spell he won one La Liga title.

He left five days after the third of those Champions League successes, vaguely citing the club’s need for change. Like so much else in his career, his motivations were opaque. But he returned the following March after the inglorious reign of Julen Lopetegui and Santi Solari’s attempt to pick up the pieces. He won another La Liga title in the two full seasons that followed.

How to assess a coach in the modern world? Two league titles in four full seasons. Three Champions Leagues in his first two and a half seasons. In another age, in another country, that would have marked Zidane as indisputably elite, but in Spain in the past decade? Domestically, his achievements feel about par.

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was viewed at Real Madrid as a head coach who let his star players like Ronaldo and Gareth Bale just be. Photograph: Matt West/BPI/Shutterstock

Madrid and Barcelona win everything, so for a Madrid coach to win half the league titles available is essentially what would be expected. But he lost eight of his first 100 games, a record. His side scored in a record 73 consecutive games. They won a joint-record 16 La Liga games in a row. They won a record 13 successive away games.

They are stats that seem unanswerable, but their accumulation has the opposite effect to that which might be expected. Zidane’s Madrid, in his first spell, were crushingly dominant. But were they dominant because of his genius or did he appear a genius because of their dominance? What comes to matter, then, is not the how many, but the how. Did Madrid win with dashing football of fitting elegance? To which the answer is, again, a shrug: they were fine.

Those three Champions League wins in a row, equally, offer surprisingly little evidence for Zidane’s greatness. Madrid have always had a tremendous capacity for achieving European success in the shadows, as though they are the default, the club that wins when nobody else is quite inspired enough to do so. Rarely has that been felt as acutely as in 2016, when they beat Roma and Wolfsburg, then edged by Manchester City on penalties in the semi-final thanks to a Fernando own goal before beating Atlético Madrid on penalties in an unmemorable final.

The following year was more impressive: the extra-time surge against Bayern and Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired demolitions of Napoli, Atlético and Juventus. But 2018 was a return to curiously ordinary success. Yes, Ronaldo and Luka Modrić were often brilliant, but there was also carelessness, notably in the quarter-final win against Juventus when they let a three-goal lead slip before a late penalty rescued them. Victory over Liverpool in the final came after a shoulder injury sustained by Mohamed Salah in a challenge with Sergio Ramos, a terrible error by a possibly injured Loris Karius and a Gareth Bale wonder goal.

View image in fullscreen Didier Deschamps was successful as head coach of France, but his side rarely captivated Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

It was hard to isolate any one moment in the success that could definitively be assigned to Zidane’s coaching genius. He didn’t create the midfield three of Casemiro, Modric and Toni Kroos. He didn’t find some new role for Ronaldo or Bale. Perhaps Zidane was some elite player whisperer, coaxing them to habitual greatness, but it was hard for an outsider to tell. Being Zidane, he was inscrutable, a cipher into which observers could read whatever message they wished.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Real Madrid coaches often run into a similar problem. They have great players. Great players do great things. Philosophies and structures always seem subservient to their talents. Ancelotti, like Zidane, has often been underappreciated, seen as somebody who essentially lets the players be. That is probably unfair and, even if it were not, perhaps that, too, is a skill. After all, plenty of coaches at Real Madrid have not been able to let the players express their innate superiority.

At the very least, it can be said that Zidane has an aura. Even those who accused him of being little more than a pair of hands clapping on the touchline must acknowledge that some hands are more authoritative than others. That may turn out to be an essential quality with France, a national team that became notorious between their two World Cup triumphs for ill-discipline, with the scandals of Seoul in 2002 and the strike at Knysna in 2010.

Whatever doubts there may be about whether Deschamps’s caution was counterproductive – until at the last, in that semi-final against Spain, he wasn’t cautious enough – over his 14 years in charge he prevented the sort of breakdowns of discipline that had undermined his predecessors, despite some extremely challenging situations.

Perhaps this is not such a troubled or troublesome France squad as some of the past decade have been, but that Zidane has taken the unusual step of banning the press from covering the arrival of players at their Clairefontaine base suggests he is eager to make a bid for control early.

His squad features a number of new faces. This is not continuity Deschamps. In the greater autonomy national coaches have compared with their club counterparts, perhaps, with France, the true nature of Zidane the coach will emerge and the great enigma will develop a face.

Sports.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
Sports.content:
Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.

Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England under-19 international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for the Sheffield United women’s team.

Olivia says the walk on Saturday, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence during the inquest. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”

A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off on Sunday at the Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day goes by where we don’t think about her.

View image in fullscreen Sheffield United and Maddy Cusack’s family paid tribute at Bramall Lane shortly after her death. Photograph: Richard Callis/MB Media/Getty Images

“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.

“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know her legacy will live on.”

The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing began belatedly on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had been set previously to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.

“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.

View image in fullscreen Maddy Cusack was also remembered during the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Newcastle. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”

Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during the 29-mile walk on Saturday, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. A fundraising page for the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected” and said: “Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”

The money is being raised for the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.

“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”

The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County left wing-back and former Derby, Sheffield United and Nottingham Forest player defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.

“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

Sports.title: Andros Townsend avoids injury after bizarre pitch roller incident in Thailand
Sports.content:
The former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away “wasn’t so bad after all” following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller.

The ex-Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker Townsend currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out before a fixture at Pattani.

Townsend was warming up when a member of staff at Pattani appeared to lose control of the pitch roller and it crashed into the 13-cap England international. The left leg of the Prachuap player briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he did feature off the bench late on in the 3-0 win.

Regular ITV pundit Townsend later took to Instagram to make light of the incident, referencing one of his recent posts in which he contrasted a sun-drenched Thai away trip with previous visits to Stoke’s windswept stadium.

Townsend said on his Instagram story: “It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad after all. Swipe to see why.”

Another post described Townsend as ‘The King of Memes in Thai League history’ and he replied “trust me” with four laughing emojis.

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum
Sports.content:
Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum

Ronald Koeman Jr was visibly emotional during a tribute to his late mother during Telstar's match against AZ Alkmaar.

The Eredivisie clash was paused in the 13th minute for an applause in honour of Bartina Koeman.



2 Koeman Jr broke down in tears during a tribute to his late mother Credit: ESPN

Her passing aged 65 was announced on Wednesday following a battle with breast cancer.

Bartina was the wife of former Netherlands captain and manager Ronald Koeman.

Tribute to Bartina Koeman

She was also Koeman Jr's mother, with the goalkeeper on the pitch for Telstar at the time of the tribute.



He could be seen wiping away tears as her picture was displayed on the big screen inside AZ's AFAS Stadion.

Supporters from both clubs paid tribute during the minute's applause.

Meanwhile, Telstar fans held sparklers aloft as they honoured Bartina's life.



Koeman Jr had joined on with the applause before using his shirt to wipe his eyes as he broke down in tears.

As the minute's applause concluded, he clapped the crowd to thank them for their tributes.



AZ went on to win the match 1-0 thanks to Mexx Meerdink's first half goal.

The result leaves Telstar 13th in the Eredivisie standings after seven matches this season.

However, they are now winless in their last six despite Koeman Jr scoring twice against Cambuur earlier this month, becoming the first goalkeeper in Eredivisie history to score two goals in one match.

The 31-year-old was making his first appearance since his mother's death was announced.



Bartina had been married to Koeman for 41 years prior to her passing, with the couple having three children together.

The former Everton manager stepped down as national team boss following their World Cup exit in order to care for her.

Announcing the tragic news on social media, Koeman wrote: "With deep sorrow, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my wonderful wife, our dearest mom and grandma.”

The news also came after Koeman Jr had welcomed the birth of his first child earlier this month.



2 A minute's applause was held in honour of Bartina during AZ's win over Telstar Credit: ESPN

Bartina was first diagnosed with breast cancer back in 2010, from which she recovered after receiving treatment.

Having recovered, the disease returned in 2018 before she was diagnosed with chronic breast cancer two years ago.

Koeman announced last year, though, that the cancer cells had spread.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero avoids red card after brutal tackle leaves Jude Bellingham writhing in pain
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero escaped being sent off for a nasty-looking challenge on Jude Bellingham in the Madrid derby.

Atletico Madrid defender Romero caught Bellingham on the knee as the Real Madrid midfielder sild in to try and tackle him.



2 VAR advised referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias to check for a possible red card for Romero Credit: ESPN

Did Romero get away with one?

Bellingham was initially booked before referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the incident.

Romero was then booked instead – but he might have been lucky not to receive stronger punishment.

Bellingham was visibly in pain after taking studs to his knee, but the England star was able to play on.



The first meeting of these two rivals saw three yellow cards in the first half alone, with Romero's centre-back teammate Marc Pubill also going into the book – along with Atletico boss Diego Simeone, just six minutes into the contest at the Estadio Metropolitano.

Real Madrid were then reduced to ten men at the start of the second half when defender Dean Huijsen was sent off with Atleti taking the lead moments later through an Alejandro Grimaldo penalty.



Romero joined Atleti this summer, arriving after a five-year spell at Tottenham, where he served as captain.

The 28-year-old was part of the Argentina squad that reached the 2026 World Cup final, losing to Spain in an ill-tempered affair.



He's featured in each of Atleti's last five games, helping them to LaLiga wins over Real Sociedad and Osasuna.

The red card comes out eventually

In the end, it was the visitors who found themselves down to 10 men.

A matter of minutes into the second half, Dean Huijsen saw red for a foul in the box, for which Atleti were awarded a penalty.

2 Huijsen was sent off with more than half an hour left to play Credit: Getty

Alex Grimaldo duly dispatched from 12 yards to break the deadlock.

And it soon got even better for the hosts, who doubled their leas through Jonathan David.



Atleti have fared well in recent home LaLiga clashes with their bitter rivals, winning two and drawing one of the last three.

Simeone's side came into this game off the back of two comprehensive league victories, keeping clean sheets in both.

Real Madrid, with Jose Mourinho back for a second spell in charge, had been in similarly good nick, winning their last three matches in all competitions.

But the first derby of the campaign looked to have got away from them during a chaotic first 15 minutes of the second half.

Sports.title: Derek McInnes achieves rare Old Firm history only matched by one Rangers manager
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes achieves rare Old Firm history only matched by one Rangers manager

Derek McInnes made history as he led Rangers to victory over Celtic in the Scottish Premiership.

Rangers' 1-0 win at Celtic Park was their second triumph over their Old Firm rivals in the space of eight days, having run out 3-0 winners at Ibrox in the League Cup last Sunday.

2 McInnes has a 100 per cent record in Old Firm games as Rangers boss so far Credit: Getty

Naderi helps McInnes make history

Ryan Naderi's first-half strike proved decisive and saw Rangers close the gap to Celtic at the top of the Premiership table to two points ahead of the first international break of the season.

And McInnes has now done something only one previous Rangers manager had ever managed.

The 55-year-old, who won the Scottish Premiership title and Scottish Cup with Rangers as a player, became the club's second boss to win both of their first Old Firm derbies in charge in all competitions.

Graeme Souness was the first to achieve that feat back in 1986, during his time as player-manager.

McInnes took over at Rangers this summer after coming agonisingly close to ending the Old Firm's 41-year grip on the Scottish title with Hearts last season.

And after a rocky start which saw them dumped out of Europa League qualifying by Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok then suffer the same fate against Czech side Jablonec in the Conference League, McInnes has overseen six straight domestic wins – with Rangers keeping five clean sheets in the process.

Rangers are chasing their first league title since the 2020/21 campaign.

They've seen Celtic win the last five on the trot, moving to a record 56 overall last term.

McInnes reflects on 'worthy win'

Speaking after Sunday's triumph, McInnes praised his team's 'big performance' – an especially impressive one given, as will be the case with all Old Firm games this season, no away fans were allowed into the ground.

"Really pleased," he told Sky Sports. "We had to deliver a big performance and we did exactly that. It's not easy coming here, the circumstances you're under and what you face.

2 Naderi scored the winning goal shortly after the half-hour mark at Celtic Park Credit: Getty

"We knew we'd have to overcome a wounded Celtic team. We played with a lot of confidence. I'm disappointed we didn't add to the goal we did score, because we were deserving of that.

"At 1-0, you still think they'll get a chance and we're kicking ourselves a wee bit that we didn't take another chance. It was a worthy win, after what was a disappointing start in the league.

"They came in with a back five, filled the middle of the pitch. In the main, we got it right. In the first 15-20 minutes, our strikers weren't giving us enough but once they started linking the play, everything looked quite calm.

"With someone like [Camilo] Duran up top, we always had to be on our toes. But it was a strong performance."

Next up for Rangers and Celtic

Rangers return to action next month with a home clash against Kilmarnock.

Celtic, meanwhile, hit the road to take on Motherwell.

The next Old Firm showdown is scheduled for January 3 at Ibrox.

Sports.title: Liverpool star ‘who doesn’t belong’ in Premier League has Andoni Iraola raging on touchline
Sports.content:
Liverpool star ‘who doesn’t belong’ in Premier League has Andoni Iraola raging on touchline

Florian Wirtz left Andoni Iraola fuming during Liverpool's clash with Bournemouth on Sunday.

The midfielder was slammed for his first half performance against the Cherries.



3 Wirtz has been told he 'doesn't belong' in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Wirtz ended the opening 45 minutes with the lowest passing accuracy of any Liverpool player.

The Germany international completed just 63 per cent of his attempted passes.

He did end up getting the assist for Alexander Isak's winner as Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0.



Deeney on Wirtz

Iraola's frustration with Wirtz on the touchline was spotted by talkSPORT's Troy Deeney.

Speaking on GameDay Live, he said: "Florian Wirtz for me, it's the first time I've seen him live.



"He just doesn't look like he belongs in this league. What I mean by that is, he's clearly talented, clearly he's got the technical ability.

"But it's like he doesn't believe he's going to score and doesn't believe he's going to impact the game. Liverpool need more from him.



"The rest of the team are starting to disbelieve because every time it goes to him, the tempo slows down.

"That means (Bradley) Barcola doesn't get the ball quick, (Cody) Gakpo doesn't get the ball quick, it allows Bournemouth to get back.

"And when they get back, it slows the whole thing down. Iraola just in front of us was absolutely blowing his top."

After Alexander Isak gave the visitors the lead following the interval, Deeney added: "His brain's working quicker than his body.



3 Wirtz had the lowest pass accuracy of any Liverpool player during the first half Credit: Getty

"He's not playing free. In the warm-up, he looks unbelievable. It looks effortless, but when he plays, he's overthinking everything."

Wirtz's Liverpool struggles

Wirtz's woes have continued into the current campaign after a difficult first season at Anfield.

The 23-year-old joined Liverpool form Bayer Leverkusen last summer for a then Premier League record £116.5million.



Despite scoring seven goals and providing nine assists in all competitions, he failed to live up to expectations for the Reds.

Wirtz is yet to register either a goal or an assist in six matches so far this term.

His last goal for the club came in a 3-1 home win over Crystal Palace on April 25.

3 Iraola was visibly frustrated with Wirtz on the touchline Credit: Getty



In contrast, his final season in Germany saw Wirtz score 16 goals and add 15 assists in 45 appearances across all competitions.

Although his current deal runs until 2030, Bayern Munich have recently been credited with an interest.

Sports.title: Pascal Gross makes statement on international future after being left out of Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Pascal Gross makes statement on international future after being left out of Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp

Pascal Gross has confirmed his retirement from international football.

The Brighton midfielder was left out of Jurgen Klopp's first Germany squad but revealed he had already made up his mind about calling time on his international career.



2 Gross earned his final cap for Germany at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Gross had 'already retired'

"Officially – since I don't have social media – I haven't announced my retirement, but I have already retired," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports.

"For me, it was over after the World Cup. I think it's time to wish the new generation nothing but the best and to keep my fingers crossed for them."

Gross, who has been one of the standout players of the Premier League season so far, earned 19 caps for Germany during a three-year international career, scoring once.



He made one appearance at both Euro 2024 and this summer's World Cup.

But he'll now focus on club football, and he's absolutely thriving for Brighton right now – having rejoined the club from Borussia Dortmund two years ago.

Scoring for fun

Gross has scored four goals and provided three assists in all competitions this term, finding the net in Brighton's superb 3-0 Premier League win over Arsenal on Saturday.



Speaking to Match of the Day after that game, Gross said he was 'loving life' right now.

"I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal," he reflected. "It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.



"We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

"I feel really good. I can't complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton – I'm loving it.

2 Gross has scored 37 goals in 252 appearances across two spells with Brighton Credit: Getty

"I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season."



Brighton sitting pretty

Brighton will head into the three-week international break no lower than fourth in the Premier League table.

Fabian Hurzeler's Seagulls have won three and drawn one of their opening five games, scoring a league-high 16 goals in the process.

They return to Premier League action next month with a trip to Sunderland, before hosting Lithuania's Kauno Zalgiris in their Conference League opener then entertaining bitter rivals Crystal Palace.

In the meantime, Germany, without Gross, begin their Nations League campaign away to the Netherlands.



Klopp was appointed in July as the successor to Julian Nagelsmann following a disappointing World Cup campaign.

Sports.title: Arsenal accused of arrogance as Brighton expose David Raya’s one flaw
Sports.content:
Arsenal's attitude has been called into question after Saturday's 3-0 defeat away to Brighton ended the Premier League champions' perfect start.

The Gunners hadn't found themselves 3-0 down in a Premier League game since May 2023 – when they also lost to Brighton by the very same scoreline, that time at home.



3 Brighton stunned Arsenal on Saturday Credit: Getty

But Mikel Arteta's side were thoroughly outclassed on the south coast, dropping points for only the third time since February and failing to win for the first time in any competition this season.

And Highbury Squad's Sophie Nicolaou wonders whether a touch of arrogance has crept in.

"Arsenal were humbled," she told Shebahn Aherne and Tony Cascarino on talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast. "And dare I say this about our team...I think we're always confident, but we're not cocky.



"And I thought yesterday we had this air of arrogance, maybe cockiness.

"I don't know if we started to believe our own hype, like this undefeated angle or whatever, but yesterday was a huge lesson in the Premier League."



Earlier, Arsenal 'Invincible' Ashley Cole had told talkSPORT he could see the current Gunners crop emulating Arsene Wenger's legendary team of 2003/04 by going the entire Premier League campaign unbeaten.

Evidently, that dream is now over for another season.

"Nothing is given to you as champions," Nicolaou continued. "People are going to come at you week after week after week.



"Every team is going to want to do that to the Arsenal, and I just don't think that we were prepared.

"And that's what I was shocked about. We looked a little arrogant. We looked like [we thought] we could go in there maybe and just turn up as champions and get that result. It was uncharacteristic across the board.

3 Arsenal had started the season with a 100 per cent record in all competitions Credit: Getty

"I'm sure Mikel is not going to be happy with that at all...I thought we kind of showed up thinking that we were going to get a result, and I just haven't seen that from our team in a long time."



Nicolaou praised Brighton for producing a 'masterclass' at the Amex Stadium, where three-time back-to-back Golden Glove-winning goalkeeper David Raya's possible sole weakness was shown up.

"They did their homework," she reflected. "It was a bit of a masterclass.

"And I also think something that they did that was interesting – that not a lot of teams do against us – is they took shots [from] outside the box [Brighton's first two goals came from range].

"And if there's one area of David Raya's game where maybe he has a little bit of a weak spot, it's taking those long shots..."



3 Raya was beaten by two shots from outside the box Credit: Getty

"So I thought the manager [Fabian Hurzeler] did brilliantly prepping for this game.

"Brighton, I thought, played their best game I've ever seen them play in the Premier League – definitely against us."

Arsenal head into the international break second in the table early in the defence of their first Premier League title for 22 years.

Sports.title: Man United star ruled out of Fulham clash in major blow to Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Man United star ruled out of Fulham clash in major blow to Michael Carrick

Benjamin Sesko is out of Manchester United's Premier League trip to Fulham on Sunday.

The striker was nowhere to be seen as Man United arrived for the train down to London on Saturday, and worries he might be injured came to pass when he wasn't named in the matchday squad.



2 Sesko scored in United's last away league game against Everton Credit: AFP

United's injury troubles

Sesko's absence will come as a significant blow to head coach Michael Carrick, who desperately needs his side to turn the corner amid a run of poor results.

United head to Craven Cottage off the back of successive home defeats to Manchester City in the Premier League and Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

And they already have a number of senior players out injured.

Luke Shaw returns to the starting 11 after missing the last three games, but long-term absentee Matthijs de Ligt is still sidelined, along with Manuel Ugarte and Tom Heaton.



Meanwhile, neither Amad nor Carlos Baleba – a summer signing from Brighton – has featured yet this season.

Baleba, however, is among the substitutes for the 4:30pm kick-off and could make his debut.



A slow start

Carrick's side find themselves 13th in the table four games into the campaign, their only win coming at home to Ipswich earlier this month.

However, victory over Fulham would take them into the top half and potentially as high as ninth.



In what is the final match before a longer than usual international break, Carrick will be demanding a big reaction from his players.

Having lost last weekend's Manchester derby in controversial fashion, United looked to be bouncing back as they took an early 2-0 lead at Old Trafford in Wednesday's Carabao Cup third-round clash with Brighton.

2 United lost from a commanding position against Brighton last time out Credit: AFP

However, they crumbled, eventually succumbing to a 3-2 defeat.

Carrick takes responsbility

Speaking ahead of the Fulham encounter, Carrick, who has faced calls to be sacked, accepted United's poor form was on him.



"That’s why I’m here," he said. "It’s my responsibility; I’m fine with that. It’s not a blame game.

"We always search for things to look at and find the blame; sometimes it gets too much of wanting to find the blame. Blame me, it’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people; it’s about finding solutions.

"It’s a whole collective thing. It’s about what you focus on really. I’m totally happy taking responsibility – no problem with that. I know where we want to get to and we want to get there fast."

United can at least take encouragement from their excellent recent record at Craven Cottage.



They've not lost their in the league since doing so in successive visits in 2009, winning eight of the last 10 such meetings.

Sports.title: Championship boss admits job is at risk as nightmare start to season continues
Sports.content:
Championship boss admits job is at risk as nightmare start to season continues

Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen concedes his job is by no means guaranteed amid the Clarets' sorry start to the season.

Eight games into the Championship campaign, Burnley have still yet to win and find themselves propping up the table.

2 Burnley have taken just four points from a possible 24 under Nicky Hayen Credit: Getty

Burnley so close to first win

It had looked like they would finally get up and running on Saturday as they led Derby for almost an hour – only to concede a stoppage-time equaliser and have to settle for a 1-1 draw.

The result leaves Burnley as one of only two teams in the whole EFL still without a league win in 2026/27.

And Hayen is well aware of 'how things go' when teams are struggling as Burnley are right now.

Hayen 'understands fans' frustration'

Asked by former Sunderland and England defender Micky Gray if he thought he would get time to turn the ship around, Hayen told talkSPORT: "I hope so. I don't know.

"I understand the frustration of the fans; I understand that they're really disappointed – also, in myself, that they're fuming. I completely understand and I know how it goes in football, but...I'm honest and I tell the truth and I'm not hiding behind it.

"There are a lot of reasons [for Burnley's poor start to the season] and you take this into account or you don't, and that's up to other people to decide...

"If we have 11 players, everyone thinks they're fit and they're fresh and they go for [it] 100 per cent, but the reality sometimes is different and you only know when you are on the inside.

"But I know I cannot claim a lot at the moment. I know that I'm responsible for it and if they [the club] make the decision that it's not good enough, then we'll see.

"But...I'm resilient; I was always a fighter. I will keep on fighting and...I'm 100 per cent sure that we can turn it around with these [next] three weeks, but we'll see what happens."

Burnley looking to bounce back

Burnley will have been hoping to mount a push for immediate promotion back to the Premier League after being relegated last season.

2 Burnley dropped more points at home to Derby on Saturday Credit: Getty

But, having appointed Hayen – who led Brugge to the 2023/24 Belgian title – as their new head coach in July following Scott Parker's departure late last term, things have not gone to plan.

In fact, Burnley have yet to manage a victory in 90 minutes in any competition.

And it's their previously resolute defence that's been the biggest issue so far: they've conceded a Championship-high 17 goals at an average of over two a game.

Burnley's sole triumph of the season so far came on penalties against Notts County in the first round of the Carabao Cup – before they were knocked out in the same way by another League One side, Bradford City, in the next round.

The Championship now hits pause until the second weekend of October for the newly extended international break.

Burnley resume their campaign away to Watford on Saturday before back-to-back home matches against Charlton and Wolves.
