World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves decline to $80.6 billion in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s foreign reserves declined to $80.63 billion at the end of July 2026, compared to $86.17 billion at the end of June and $97.432 billion at the end of 2025.

Foreign reserves in US dollars fell by roughly $16.79 billion in the first seven months of 2026 compared to the end of 2025, representing a reduction of nearly 17.2 percent.

The value of foreign reserves in Iraqi dinars declined to 104.82 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $80.19 billion) at the end of July, compared to 112.02 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $85.7 billion) at the end of June and 126.66 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $96.9 billion) at the end of 2025.

The value of gold reserves saw a slight increase to 29.66 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $22.7 billion) at the end of July, compared to 29.41 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $22.5 billion) at the end of June, but remained below their level at the end of 2025, which was 31.48 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $24.08 billion).

The CBI’s investments declined to 75.03 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $57.4 billion) at the end of July, compared to 81.99 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $62.7 billion) at the end of June and 93.26 trillion Iraqi dinars ($71.34 billion) at the end of 2025.

Cash reserves held in the CBI’s vaults also decreased to 124 billion Iraqi dinars ($94.86 million) at the end of July, compared to 614 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $470 million) at the end of June and 1.9 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1.45 billion) at the end of 2025.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit three million barrels in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

Data indicates that Iraq’s oil exports continue to be affected by the repercussions of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, despite improved export routes in the past few weeks. Baghdad is working to secure alternatives and enhance the operational capacity of its oil terminals.

Despite a relative improvement, Iraq’s current oil exports remain below pre-February 2026 levels, reflecting continued pressure on supply chains, after shipments reached approximately 73 million barrels in August, according to data released by Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

The average daily export volume of Iraqi oil in August 2026 surged to approximately 2.354 million barrels. This figure represents a significant increase compared to the combined total of roughly 526,470 barrels per day in May and June. This rise marks the highest levels of oil export and revenue since the onset of the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Iraq’s oil exports during August were distributed between the country’s southern maritime terminals and the Turkish port of Ceyhan via the northern outlet.

The increase in exports comes amid an easing of shipping delays in the Arabian Gulf and Iran’s authorization for certain oil tankers transporting Iraqi oil to traverse the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s oil exports indicate a notable recovery compared to previous months, with revenues reaching approximately $4.5 billion in August, compared to $2.336 billion in May and June combined.

World.title: Six French ISIS suspects face trial in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi court launched on Sunday the trial of six French nationals suspected of membership in the terrorist group ISIS.

A member of the Supreme Judicial Council warned that the suspects might face the death sentence if convicted of crimes against Iraq and its people.

According to two court legal sources, the defendants were among 47 French ISIS inmates relocated from prisons in northeast Syria in 2025 as part of an operation authorized by US forces and Iraqi officials.

According to Reuters, officials from the French embassy in Iraq were present at the Baghdad criminal court.

The six inmates being tried under Iraq’s counter-terrorism law arrived in the court in a prison van accompanied by a convoy of Humvees carrying Iraqi Special Forces officers.

The suspects were wearing yellow prison jumpsuits.

The judge in charge postponed the hearing until October 5 to allow defense lawyers to study the case files.

Abbas al-Maliki, a court-appointed solicitor for one of the prisoners, told Reuters that his client was facing allegations of ISIS membership.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

Earlier this month, the Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq announced that it officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

World.title: Iraq opens restricted air zones for civilian aviation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has lifted its decade-long military restrictions on western airspace, returning full control to civilian authorities.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport announced on Friday that it has fully eliminated the restricted zones, thereby restoring complete sovereignty over the country’s airspace.

Iraq’s General Company for Air Navigation Services (GCANS) now controls all previously restricted military zones, which range from the northern province of Nineveh to the southern desert in Anbar province.

Between 2016 and 2017, the airspace was restricted to civilian planes. The Iraqi Air Force and the US-led international coalition used it only for combat missions against ISIS.

The decision would enable foreign airlines to use shorter and more efficient international flight corridors. The decision is expected to reduce operational rates for global airlines and simultaneously boost transit charge revenue for the Iraqi government.

The Transport Ministry in Iraq announced that the removal of these restrictions is part of the withdrawal process, as Iraq and the United States work together to coordinate the departure of the US-led international coalition’s remaining forces.

Technical and legal alignment for completely integrating the newly available routes into civilian flight is projected to be completed by October 1, 2026.

World.title: US dollar eases below 160,000 IQD across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar experienced a slight retreat across parallel currency exchanges in Iraq on Sunday, September 20, 2026, dipping marginally below the 160,000-dinar mark recorded over the weekend while continuing to trade at a substantial premium above the official state benchmark.

According to market data, parallel bureaus across major trading hubs posted quotes well above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100.

In the capital city of Baghdad, exchange bureaus quoted selling rates at 159,750 dinars per $100, with buying rates settling at 159,000 dinars.

Trading across northern financial desks in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a slightly softer posture, posting selling prices of 158,700 dinars per $100 against buying levels of 158,250 dinars. In the southern economic hub of Basra, rates closely aligned with northern counters, recording 159,000 dinars for sale and 158,500 dinars for purchase.

While the day’s trades reflect a fractional cooling of roughly 250 to 950 dinars compared to Saturday’s peak surges, currency desks continue to price in significant liquidity risk.

The persistent spread between the parallel exchanges and the statutory peg highlights ongoing domestic cash-flow constraints and defensive trading behavior among market participants ahead of the critical September 30 deadline.

World.title: Washington Institute urges sanctions on Maliki and Ameri over disarmament delays
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A policy analysis published by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy has recommended that the United States prepare targeted individual sanctions against former Iraqi Prime Minister Nouri Al-Maliki and Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Ameri if both figures continue obstructing federal efforts to disarm armed factions.

The study, authored by former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State David Schenker and reported by the 964 Network, argues that the two veteran political leaders—who collectively command 47 parliamentary seats within the ruling Coordination Framework—remain entrenched in maximalist positions rather than facilitating genuine state control over weapons, particularly following high-profile cross-border drone strikes against regional energy targets.

The analysis highlights that while Al-Maliki previously pledged to defuse factional tensions and avert collisions with Baghdad’s sovereign agenda, Iranian-backed groups within the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) subsequently launched an explosive drone barrage on September 10 targeting Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude pipeline near Yanbu, Riyadh, and Medina.

The assault, which temporarily disrupted up to 4–5 million barrels per day of transit to the Red Sea, directly undermined Coordination Framework claims of having neutralized escalation risks, exposing the fragility of domestic political assurances.

Schenker notes that Al-Maliki narrowly escaped U.S. Treasury designations during the first Trump administration and warns that continued efforts to replace disarmament with ambiguous “containment” models—akin to Lebanese political formulas surrounding Hezbollah—should trigger direct U.S. financial designations against both Al-Maliki and Al-Ameri.

The policy paper comes as Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi approaches his self-imposed September 30 deadline to monopolize arms under sovereign command—a date that coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the U.S.-led International Coalition’s mission in Iraq.

While moderate factions like Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq and Kata’ib Imam Ali offered preliminary disarmament concessions, and Muqtada Al-Sadr agreed to absorb Saraya Al-Salam into the regular military, hardline elements led by Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harakat Hezbollah Al-Nujaba, and Kata’ib Sayyid Al-Shuhada have openly resisted.

Bolstered by summer visits from IRGC Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani, these groups have conditioned disarmament on non-starter demands, including dissolving the constitutionally recognized Kurdish Peshmerga, expelling Turkish forces, and enshrining PMF benefits by statute, while proposing unacceptable workarounds such as storing heavy weaponry in Iran or maintaining private depots under a nominal two-year activity freeze.

World.title: Iraq’s University of Technology explores academic partnerships in Spain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s University of Technology conducted high-level academic discussions on Saturday, September 19, 2026, with Spain’s University of Seville and University of Granada, aiming to broaden bilateral research cooperation, facilitate student and faculty exchanges, and launch joint scientific projects.

According to an official university statement carried by INA, the institutional visit was led by the President of the University of Technology, Mohsen Nouri Hamza, heading a senior academic delegation as part of the institution’s broader strategy to expand global academic engagement.

At the University of Granada, Hamza met with University Rector Pedro Mercado Pacheco to review frameworks for institutional collaboration and advance a draft comprehensive Global Agreement designed to govern future academic and scientific ties.

The delegation held additional technical sessions with Irene Pedreira Romero, Director of International Projects and Networks, and Leandro Di Stasi, Director of Internationalization at the International School for Postgraduate Studies.

Deliberations centered on establishing joint research initiatives and leveraging opportunities under the European Union’s Erasmus+ program to facilitate bilateral mobility for researchers, instructors, and graduate students, including hosting Iraqi postgraduate candidates in Spanish laboratories to carry out specialized thesis work.

The mission to the University of Seville focused on technical and engineering disciplines aligned with national development priorities. Talks concentrated on joint projects in renewable energy, industrial catalysts, advanced materials, structural engineering, and sustainable architectural design.

The Iraqi delegation—which included Dean of the College of Architecture Abbas Ali Hamza, Dean of the College of Electromechanical Engineering Ghassan Abdul Hussein Bilal, Materials Engineering faculty member Mohammed Al-Zuhairi, and Electromechanical Engineering faculty member Sundus Samir Jumaa—agreed to establish specialized bilateral research teams aimed at supporting sustainable development through academic innovation.

World.title: Four key clashes conclude Iraq Stars League matchday 8 on Saturday
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Four decisive fixtures will wrap up Matchday 8 of the Iraq Stars League on Saturday evening, September 19, 2026, setting the stage for high-stakes clashes spanning the title chase, mid-table consolidation, and redemption campaigns.

The evening action kicks off at 6:45 PM Baghdad time with two simultaneous fixtures. Ghaz Al-Shamal takes on Newroz in an encounter where both clubs will battle to secure maximum points and strengthen their footholds in the league standings. At the same hour, perennial title contenders Al-Quwa Al-Jawiya meet Diyala, determined to bounce back from recent dropped points, rediscover winning form, and reignite their domestic momentum.

The focus shifts to the summit of the table at 9:00 PM when league leaders Al-Karma host Zakho at Al-Jawlan Stadium. Al-Karma enters the contest intent on protecting their prime position at the top of the standings and sustaining their strong run of form, while Zakho aims to disrupt the leaders and secure a valuable away result to bolster their points tally.

Matchday 8 concludes at 9:30 PM with Al-Shorta welcoming Al-Kahrabaa at Al-Shorta Stadium. Returning swiftly to domestic duties following their midweek AFC Champions League Two continental fixture, the hosts will target all three points in front of home supporters, while an ambitious Al-Kahrabaa side seeks to capitalize on any fatigue to claim an upset.

World.title: BJP, Congress trade barbs over PM Modi mimicry at Rahul Gandhi’s Indore event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday criticised the Congress after stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani mimicked Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event attended by party leader Rahul Gandhi in Madhya Pradesh, with Union ministers and other BJP leaders targeting the opposition party and Congress MP over the performance.

The comedian performed the skit with the Rae Bareli MP during the latest edition of the âChhatron Ki Goonjâ event in Indore on Saturday. A video of the performance was shared by the Congress on X.

In the short act, Mani came on stage laughing and hugged Rahul. âMy friend. How are you?â he said. The Congress leader replied, âI'm fine; how are you, Modi ji?â Mani responded, âGreat harassmentâ, and continued laughing while repeatedly using the phrase âmy friendâ.

Rahul then said, âVery nice to meet you,â and asked Mani to âtell me moreâ. The comedian continued laughing and hugging Gandhi before saying, âMaa ko kursi do, maaâ, while pointing towards the audience.

BJP leaders hit out at Rahul Gandhi

Union minister Piyush Goyal reacted to the performance on X, calling Rahul âAsanskari naraz fufa (uncultured disgruntled uncle).â

âThe irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji's name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me,â Goyal said, asking the former Congress president to âlook in the mirrorâ.





Union minister Kiren Rijiju also criticised Rahul, saying, âI hadn't imagined that a party which was in power for nearly six decades would turn into such a circus that is busy entertaining their own shrunken supporters.â

Rijiju said Indians were proud that Prime Minister Modi was the âmost popularâ elected leader in the world.

âCongress party has become a party of comedians and Jokers! They are out forever.... RIP,â he said.

âDo you feel absolutely no shame in mocking an elderly mother and the Prime Minister of India?â Rijiju asked Rahul, while posting a video of PM Modi in which the prime minister is seen asking for a chair for an elderly woman who had attended one of his programmes.

BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani also reacted to the controversy, writing in Hindi on X, âJab nash manuj per chata hai, pehle vivek mar jaata haiâ (When doom looms over a person, it's his conscience that dies first).

BJP national secretary Sandeep Pathak called the mimicry act an expression of âdesperationâ and the âgrowing intellectual bankruptcyâ of the Congress.

âWhen you lose touch with India's values, you lose touch with India itself. And that is precisely where the Congress has lost its way,â Pathak, a Rajya Sabha MP, said on X.

Congress leaders defend programme

Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel hit back at the BJP's criticism, saying every person's mother deserved respect and questioning why similar concerns were not raised when the mothers of Rahul and other leaders were allegedly insulted.

âEveryone's mother is a mother, not PM Modi's mother alone. Why are their feelings not hurt when they insult Rahul Gandhi's mother or other leaders' mothers? This culture of insulting mothers was started by BJP-RSS and Mahamanav,â Baghel said.

Congress MP Imraan Masood said the âChhatron Ki Goonjâ programme had âshattered eardrumsâ of BJP leaders.

âLet the elections come. They will find out soon enough. 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' has shattered their eardrums.

They see Rahul Gandhi in their dreams and wake up with a start,â Masood said in Ranchi.

Congress leader TS Singh Deo said criticism and mimicry should not be objected to, but opposed the use of abusive language in public conversations.

âI do not think it is acceptable to stoop to the level of abusive language in a public conversation. But beyond that, if you're criticising someone in a normal way, even in a joking manner or with mimicry, no one should have any objection to it,â he said in Raipur.

World.title: Healthcare goes digital: When doctors go behind the app wall, who gets left behind?
World.content:
What if your phone becomes the first thing you need to see a doctor?

As healthcare increasingly moves from hospital counters and paper records to apps and online portals, access to care is becoming closely tied to access to technology.

For many patients, digital healthcare can mean quicker consultations, easier access to medical records and fewer trips to hospitals. But for others, particularly older people, rural communities, low-income families and those with limited digital literacy, the shift can add another layer of difficulty.

The problem is not simply whether a person owns a smartphone. Patients may struggle with internet connectivity, downloading and navigating apps, remembering passwords and OTPs, uploading documents or understanding information presented online.

In many households, a single smartphone is shared by several family members, while caregivers often become the bridge between patients and digital health services.

As government and private healthcare services increasingly encourage, and in some cases require, people to use digital platforms, a larger question is emerging: Is technology making healthcare more accessible, or creating a new barrier to accessing it?

Difficulties patients might face despite digital help

When the smartphone becomes the gateway to healthcare

Digital health has opened up several ways for patients to manage their care remotely.





People can consult doctors online, monitor blood sugar through connected devices, receive medication and appointment reminders, and access diet and educational resources without making frequent hospital visits.

Telemedicine became particularly important during the Covid-19 pandemic, when lockdowns made physical consultations difficult. But the experience also exposed how uneven access to digital healthcare could be.

A DIG-EQUITY study published in

The Times of India

, examining the experiences of people with diabetes, caregivers, healthcare providers, policymakers and community organisations in urban and rural Tamil Nadu, found significant differences in how people used digital health services.

Younger patients were generally more comfortable with smartphones, health applications and teleconsultations, while many older people needed family members to book appointments, join consultations or access medical reports.

For some, physical limitations added to the problem. Impaired vision or hearing, as well as difficulty handling smartphones, could make navigating digital platforms harder.

Even among younger people, digital access did not automatically translate into a preference for online care. Some people with type 1 diabetes continued to prefer in-person consultations because of the need for physical examinations.

The digital divide is also closely linked to where people live and what they can afford.

Urban patients are more likely to have reliable internet connections, smartphones and access to digital services. A study published in

Nature

, examining barriers to digital health transformation in India, found that the challenges went beyond simply having a smartphone or internet connection.

The study identified poor network coverage and inadequate IT infrastructure, the high cost of devices and digital systems, a lack of technical expertise, language and communication barriers, and difficulties faced by users among the major challenges.

For patients, these barriers can have very practical consequences. The study noted that some had to rely on family members' smartphones to attend teleconsultations, while the cost of smart devices could limit access to mobile health applications.

The findings suggest that digital access cannot be measured simply by whether someone owns a phone. Reliable connectivity, affordability, digital skills, language accessibility and the availability of human support all influence whether a patient can actually use digital healthcare.

That distinction becomes particularly important as healthcare services increasingly move online. Putting a service on a digital platform does not automatically make it accessible to everyone.

Who gets left behind?

ABHA and the push towards connected healthcare

India's digital health infrastructure is expanding rapidly. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), through platforms such as ABHA, is aimed at creating a connected digital health ecosystem, while eSanjeevani has widened access to telemedicine.

With hundreds of millions of ABHA IDs created and telemedicine consultations running into hundreds of millions, the scale of this shift is significant.

But the benefits of digital healthcare are not evenly experienced.

The gap becomes particularly visible when digital systems are introduced at the hospital level. For some patients, the shift has not removed queues; it has created an additional one.

Rekha (name changed), a patient at the Delhi National Cancer Institute, said patients earlier had to wait in a single OPD queue, with doctors arriving around 8am.

According to her, the process now involves generating a token through the ABHA app before reaching the hospital, followed by another number at the reception.

âEarlier there used to be only one OPD line and the doctors used to arrive at 8am. Now they have made it mandatory to download the ABHA app and apply for a token number. Then we get another number from reception, and doctors arrive at 10am. Several patients need immediate care, but this extra queue has made life a bit more difficult,â she said.

Delhi National Cancer Institute (pic credit: Priyanka Jaiswal)

For those without a smartphone or reliable internet connection, Rekha said the process can begin hours before they reach the doctor. Some patients, she said, arrive around midnight or 1am and spend the night waiting because they cannot access the network or generate a digital token.

Those with smartphones may apply through the ABHA app around 5am and reach the hospital by 7am, she said, only to wait again at reception before seeing a doctor later in the morning.

Dr Manisha Arora, Director, Internal Medicine, CK Birla Hospital, Delhi, said ABHA should remain a facilitator rather than become a gateway to treatment.

âA patient should never feel that access to technology determines access to healthcare,â she said, noting that patients without an ABHA ID, smartphone or internet connectivity should continue to be able to register physically and receive the same clinical care.

She stressed that hospitals should adopt a digital-first, not digital-only, approach.

âThat means retaining manual registration counters, providing assisted kiosks and having dedicated digital-support personnel, particularly for elderly and first-time users.â

Insurance goes digital, but payment and paperwork remain a burden

Digital insurance processes are another area where patients can struggle. Families dealing with hospitalisation may simultaneously have to navigate e-KYC, pre-authorisation, co-payments, deductions and non-payable items.

Manivannan Selvaraj, Founder and Managing Director, Kauvery Group of Hospitals, said translating a clinical treatment plan into a pre-authorisation submission, and then managing the queries and follow-ups that come back, involves a long chain of steps that a patient is neither equipped nor educated to handle, and should not have to handle while they or a family member is unwell.

âSometimes delays or claim issues arise because documentation is incomplete rather than because of a medical concern,â Arora said, stressing that hospital insurance desks need to act as patient counsellors, explaining the process rather than merely uploading documents.

âTrue digital accessibility is when technology works in the background and the patient still experiences a human interface at the front,â she said.

What's the solution?

At 65, Amarnath (name changed) has an insurance policy but says managing it digitally has become difficult. He is often unsure about when he can claim, when premiums are due and how to complete the process online, leaving his son to handle the details for him.

âI have an insurance policy, but I often donât know when I can make a claim, when the premium is due or how to complete these processes online.

My son manages it for me. At my age, it is not always easy to visit a centre every time I need to check my policy or make a claim. If healthcare is becoming digital, these services should also be made accessible to elderly people, so that we can manage them ourselves without having to depend on others,â he said.

He also highlighted how the growing use of digital payments in hospitals can create another challenge for elderly patients unfamiliar with the technology.

Having a UPI-enabled phone does not necessarily mean being comfortable using it, particularly during a medical emergency when payments may need to be made quickly.

âI have UPI on my phone, but for people of our generation, it is difficult to become fully comfortable with the process and make an immediate payment, especially during a health emergency. This is something that should also be addressed,â he said.

Covid era showed that systems still struggle

The pandemic offered an early and stark example of how closely technology and healthcare had become intertwined.

While telemedicine and digital systems helped patients access services during lockdowns, other parts of the healthcare chain showed that digitisation alone could not solve problems of capacity and access.

As reported by

The Times of India

earlier, delays in Covid testing became a major concern during the second wave. Udham Singh, 22, developed high fever, severe cough, body ache and breathlessness after his sample was collected for an RT-PCR test.

His report, which confirmed Covid infection, came several days after the sample was taken.

âI would have landed in an ICU had I waited for some more time. The element of uncertainty due to delay also caused extreme mental trauma,â Singh said.

For patients waiting at home, the delay was not merely an inconvenience. It affected decisions about treatment and isolation. Some families also faced difficulties maintaining quarantine while waiting for test results.

Priya Jaiswal, a resident of Old Delhi, recalled how a network outage during the pandemic left her dependent on officials for essential medicines. With her internet connection down, she could not use UPI to make payments or order medicines online, leaving her waiting for officials to arrive at her home.

âWe had to wait for hours for officials to arrive and hand over the medicines while we were in quarantine. Even online consultations became difficult because of continuous power cuts at a time when we needed healthcare the most,â she said.

The surge in demand for Covid testing also put pressure on government laboratories to issue digital reports on time, highlighting another challenge for digital healthcare: a digital interface is only as effective as the system supporting it.

Covid-19 vaccination certificates also affected people's travel and employment plans.

Covid-19 highlights struggle

Varghese Thomas, a youth from the city, told TOI that five people in his group had taken their first vaccine dose around the same time, but only one had received the certificate nearly 40 days later.

âWhen we applied for jobs, prospective employers were asking us about the vaccination. They wanted us to produce the certificate,â he said.

Registering through Co-WIN was another difficulty for people in rural areas.

As reported by

The Times of India

earlier, 68-year-old Adhi Kesavan from Gudiyattam in Tamil Nadu's Vellore district had to travel around 5-7 km with his wife to a common service centre to register for vaccination.

Kesavan did not own a smartphone or know how to use one. He was directed to the centre by his panchayat head, who told him that his details could be registered there and that the hospital would contact him when a vaccine became available.

âI heard from our panchayat head that we can get vaccinated if we register at the e-sevai maiyyam. Our number will be given to the hospitals nearby and we will get a call once the vaccine is ready,â Kesavan said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He was still waiting for that call.

Digital healthcare cannot mean digital-only healthcare

India's digital-health expansion will ultimately be measured not only by how many people are connected to the system, but also by whether those who are not can still access care with the same ease and dignity.

The goal should not be to make healthcare digital at any cost. It should be to make healthcare more accessible, using technology when it helps, and providing human support when it doesn't.

Because for a patient struggling to connect, navigate an app, remember an OTP or make a digital payment, the smartphone should never become another obstacle between them and a doctor.

World.title: 'Can't stop BJP alone': Owaisi opens alliance door to 'like-minded' parties in UP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh set for assembly polls in 2027,

supremo

has thrown open the possibility of an alliance with parties looking to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third straight term, saying no opposition party can take on the BJP alone.

Owaisi, speaking to news agency ANI on Sunday, invited âlike-mindedâ parties for talks and said AIMIM was prepared to work with them if the common objective was to keep the BJP out of power.

âWe do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone,â he said.

His outreach comes as political parties begin preparing for the 2027 contest in Uttar Pradesh, where the BJP has been in power since 2017 under the leadership of

.

Owaisi, however, cautioned against viewing the coming election through the lens of previous polls, saying the political contest would have its own set of challenges.

âAssembly elections are coming. It wonât be the 2014 election, nor the 2017 election, nor the 2019 election, nor the 2022 election.





This is going to be a completely different election,â he said.

âWe asked for six seatsâ in Bihar

Owaisi pointed to AIMIMâs experience in Bihar to underline the partyâs position on alliances. He said the party had approached several opposition leaders before the

Bihar elections

, seeking an alliance and asking for six seats, but the proposal did not find support.

âWe said this in Bihar as well, and our president, Akhtarul Iman, wrote a letter not just to the RJD or the Congress, but to all the CPI and Communist Party leaders.

We said, âPlease give us six seats.â But they did not agree,â he said.

Despite the lack of an alliance, Owaisi said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh. He claimed the partyâs leadership had developed from the grassroots and said its workers were already active across constituencies.

âOur party organisation has become quite strong. Our leadership has emerged at the grassroots level, and our leaders have a strong connection with the ground.

The party is working hard on its part,â he said.

Hyderabad MP said alliance talks would not determine AIMIMâs organisational plans.

âWhether we are in talks with whom or not is a different matter, but we will continue our work. If you want to stop the BJP, come and talk to us. We are ready to work with you,â he said.

Owaisi targets BJP, SP over âhooliganismâ

Turning to the Yogi-led BJP government, Owaisi alleged that several promises made by the party remained unfulfilled.

He raised issues including governance, law and order, electricity and land disputes, saying these would become important themes in the election.

He also criticised the previous

Samajwadi Party

government, drawing a comparison between the two regimes.

âWhen the Samajwadi Party was in power, one kind of hooliganism used to happen. Someone else did it. Now, under their government, a different kind of hooliganism is happening,â Owaisi said.

He also sought the public release of the SIT report into the alleged Ram Mandir embezzlement case and questioned how accused persons were securing bail.

âWhy isnât the SIT report released to the public? Why doesnât the government release it? And why are those people getting bail? How are they getting bail? Itâs strange. This will also be a big talking point,â he said.

He said he was in Kanpur on Sunday and would visit Shravasti in six days, followed by Azamgarh. Public meetings are also planned in three or four constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh.

World.title: Not just Rekha Gupta and Arvind Kejriwal: LK Advani, Manish Sisodia issued notices in Delhi SIR
World.content:
SIR notices issued to LK Advani, Manish Sisodia

From politicians to bureaucrats, thousands face verification over 'discrepancies' in SIR enumeration forms

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP stalwart LK Advani and former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia are among the prominent voters whose names figure in the list of 33 lakh people being issued notices over âlogical discrepanciesâ in details furnished during the recent Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi.âThe notices arose from âlogical discrepanciesâ in the details furnished in their enumeration forms. Their names will be included in the final electoral rolls after due process of verification of facts and documents to be furnished by such voters,â a senior poll officer told PTI, confirming that notices had been issued to both Advani and Sisodia.âThe process of verification of facts and documents is underway and validation of entries is being done accordingly,â the officer added.The 98-year-old Advani, a former deputy prime minister, his daughter Pratibha and daughter-in-law Geetika also received notices after their names could not be mapped to the 2002 SIR electoral roll. His son, Jayant, however, cleared the mapping exercise.All four are registered voters in the New Delhi assembly constituency.Meanwhile, in Sisodiaâs family, his wife Seema and son Meer have also been issued notices.While the Election Commission has not cited a specific reason for the notice issued to the AAP leader, his son Meerâs notice mentions a âdiscrepancy in his parentâs nameâ, according to officials. The notice issued to his wife, Seema, cites a âmismatch in her own nameâ.Many prominent voters, including senior government functionaries, bureaucrats and politicians, have been issued notices as part of the SIR exercise in Delhi.Chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal and former Union minister Kapil Sibal have also received notices over similar discrepancies, officials said.Guptaâs entry was validated following verification of her documents, and her name has been cleared for inclusion in the final electoral roll of the Shalimar Bagh constituency, scheduled to be published on November 4.According to the Delhi CEOâs office, notices are being issued to voters whose names could not be linked to the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR, or whose details showed discrepancies when matched against the earlier roll.As part of the door-to-door verification exercise conducted between June 30 and August 17, every voter was required to submit an enumeration form.Of the around 97 lakh voters included in the draft electoral rolls, 33.13 lakh have been identified for notices over discrepancies in their enumeration forms. More than 31.63 lakh notices have been served so far.Most of the notices relate to the absence of corresponding records in the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR in 2002.Voters have been asked to submit their replies along with supporting documents to the Electoral Registration Officers of their respective Assembly constituencies by October 29.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins women in traditional Chachani dance during Badrinath visit
World.content:
Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins women in traditional Chachani dance during Badrinath visit

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BADRINATH: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday joined local women in a traditional Chachdance at Bamani village near Badrinath during his visit to the shrine, interacting with residents and getting a glimpse of the region's local traditions.During his visit, CM Dhami also stopped at a local shop in Badrinath Dham, where he savoured milk and jalebi. He interacted with local residents and pilgrims who had arrived at the shrine.The chief minister also attended the Shri Badrinath Katha Mahotsav being organised near the Shri Narayan Swami Temple on Narayan Palace Road in Badrinath.Dhami's visit comes amid a series of religious and cultural activities being held in Badrinath as the second phase of the Char Dham pilgrimage is underway following the monsoon season.Earlier on Sunday, Dhami offered prayers at Shri Badrinath Dham and sought the blessings of Shri Badri Vishal for the prosperity and well-being of Uttarakhand and its people.Speaking about the ongoing pilgrimage, Dhami said the first phase had been historic and set a new record, with approximately 51 lakh pilgrims and devotees having already offered prayers."By the grace of Baba Kedar and all our holy shrines, the first phase of the pilgrimage has been truly historic, setting a new record.Approximately 51 lakh pilgrims and devotees have already offered their prayers, and the second phase of the pilgrimage is now underway following the monsoon season," he said.The chief minister said arrangements had been put in place to ensure smooth travel and convenient darshan for pilgrims, adding that roadwork along the pilgrimage routes was also underway.He also said work on the master plan for Lord Badri Vishal was progressing rapidly, while acknowledging the challenges posed by the limited construction season in the high-altitude region.The visit also coincides with the two-day Devbhoomi Cultural Festival being held in Badrinath on September 19 and 20 under Operation Sadbhavana. The festival, organised jointly by the Indian Army and Chamoli district administration, is showcasing Uttarakhand's folk dances, music, handicrafts, local products and traditional cuisine. Women-led self-help groups, artisans, farmers and young entrepreneurs are also participating in the event.The cultural festival is being held with the theme "Our Heritage, Our Future" and aims to provide a platform for local traditions, products and talent from the border regions while connecting younger generations with Uttarakhand's cultural heritage.

World.title: BJP leaders slam mimicry of PM at Rahul Gandhi’s student event
World.content:
A political row erupted in Madhya Pradesh on Sunday (September 20, 2026), as BJP leaders slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for featuring the mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi by standup comedian Pulkit Mani at a student interaction event in Indore.

Mr. Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, could be seen laughing during the performance by Mr. Mani at his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event. In the act, Mr. Mani appeared to be mimicking Mr. Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders and others. While Mr. Mani did not name the Prime Minister in his act, Mr. Gandhi said, “How are you, Modi ji?”, while hugging him.

Another part of the act, where Mr. Mani appeared to be mocking the Prime Minister for asking for a chair for an elderly woman at a rally, took the most heat. Similar performances by the comedian have previously gone viral on social media.

‘Insulting honour of mothers’

Soon after the event, Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav shared a clip of the act and said that Mr. Gandhi’s attitude was “extremely shameful”.

“This irresponsible attitude of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is extremely shameful, condemnable, and unbecoming. By insulting the honour of our country’s culture and mothers, he has encouraged leading the youth’s future in the wrong direction,” Mr. Yadav wrote on X, late on September 19.

“Our visionary Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, who had set an exemplary example by placing the honour of mothers above all, is being mocked in this manner, which is an insult to mothers across the country,” he said, seeking an apology from the Congress.

‘Cheap political theatre’

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said the act amounted to “cheap political theatre”.

“Uncultured angry uncle! The irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji’s name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me. Look in the mirror, Mr. Rahul Gandhi,” Mr. Goyal said on X.

Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai invoked the Delhi University Student Union (DUSU) election results to take a dig at Mr. Gandhi’s event, claiming that the ABVP’s victory showed that the youth of the country was with the BJP.

PM’s previous mockery unearthed

While the Congress is yet to officially respond to the BJP’s allegations, sources say that many within the party did not “approve of it”.

However, various Congress supporters on social media shared an old clip of Mr. Modi’s interaction with students from 2019, in which he was apparently seen mocking Mr. Gandhi as a dyslexic person.

While interacting by video conference with a group of students gathered at IIT-Kharagpur, Mr. Modi had interrupted a student who was explaining how her project could help dyslexic kids and laughingly asked if it could also help “40 to 50-year-old child as well”.

As the girl said, “Yes, it can,” Mr. Modi further added, “Then the mother of such children will get very happy.” His comments, which drew laughter from the audience, were seen as potshots at Mr. Gandhi.

At his event in Indore, Mr. Gandhi had alleged that a “system” run by a handful of powerful people like Mr. Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a few bureaucrats and businesspersons had captured the country, harming students and the education system. He claimed that the “system” did not want students who raised questions and preferred “andhbhakts (blind followers)” instead.

Following the controversy, Mr. Mani said in an Instagram story that an upcoming show of his, scheduled to be held in Uttar Pradesh’s Noida, has been cancelled “due to unforeseen circumstances”. Gautam Budh Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, under whose jurisdiction Noida falls, was not available for a comment on Sunday evening, while some other district officials said that they were not aware of the show or any decision regarding it.

World.title: Kurmis to be kept out of UCC, says West Bengal CM; promises to withdraw old cases
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (September 20, 2026) said the Kurmi community would be kept outside the ambit of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) and announced that cases registered against members of the community during protests under the previous Trinamool Congress government would be withdrawn.

The Kurmis are a prominent community in the State’s Jangalmahal region. They are currently categorised as Other Backward Class and have been demanding the status of Scheduled Tribe (ST).

Members of the Kurmi community had organised road and railway blockades across parts of West Bengal during the previous Trinamool Congress government’s tenure, demanding ST status and inclusion of the Kurmali language in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Mr. Adhikari also promised to push for constitutional recognition of the Kurmali and Rajbanshi languages.

The West Bengal government has said it would submit a “Further Common Justification Report” to the Centre to support the inclusion of the Kurmi community in the ST list.

Committee on UCC

On the UCC, the State government has set up a committee led by former Supreme Court judge Ranjana Gopal Desai to work out the modalities for implementing the proposed code in the State. The government has already promised to keep ST out of the ambit of the UCC.

Addressing a Karam festival programme in Purulia, the Chief Minister said that many leaders of the Kurmi community had approached him seeking to keep the community out of the ambit of the UCC.

Mr. Adhikari accused the previous government of creating divisions within the Kurmi community and said his government would fulfil the promises made in its election manifesto.

“The previous government (in West Bengal) created divisions among the Kurmis... It never wanted them to stay united. We will, on the other hand, keep all promises made to the community in our ‘Sankalp Patra’ before this year’s Assembly elections,” he said.

The Chief Minister said people of the region had voted for the BJP over the past several years and assured to protect the region’s language, diversity and natural resources.

Criticising the previous administration, he alleged that it had been “selling hills” and promised that no natural resources would be auctioned under his tenure.

“It is our responsibility to protect the dignity of language, culture, tradition and rights. The previous government was even selling hills! I promised not to let anyone touch any of them. I will not let anyone touch the gifts of nature. No mountain can be auctioned,” he said. Mr. Adhikari also announced an allocation of ₹50 crore for the Kurmi Development Board and said the amount would be increased if necessary.

Several members of the Kurmi community, including prominent leader Ajit Mahato and Purulia BJP MP Jyotirmoy Singh Mahato, attended the festival.

World.title: IPS officers Kanthi Rana Tata, Vishal Gunni get postings after revocation of suspension
World.content:
The State government on Sunday transferred and posted several IPS officers, including 2004-batch officer Kanthi Rana Tata and 2005-batch officer Vishal Gunni, who were suspended in connection with the actress Kadambari Jethwani case. The rejig also included the appointment of new Superintendents of Police (SPs) for three districts.

The government had recently revoked the suspension of Mr. Tata, who was Commissioner of Police, Vijayawada, and Mr. Gunni, who was serving as Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Vijayawada. They had faced allegations of illegally confining and harassing Ms. Jethwani and her family in connection with a case. Both officers had been awaiting postings after their suspension was revoked.

On Sunday evening, the government issued orders posting Mr. Tata as Inspector General of Police, Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety. Mr. Gunni was posted as Deputy Inspector General of Police, Training, in the existing vacancy and given full additional charge as Director of the Andhra Pradesh Police Academy (APPA) until further orders.

Meanwhile, 2005-batch officer C.M. Thrivikram Varma, who was serving as Director General of the Special Protection Force, was transferred and posted as Inspector General of Police and Director, Forensic Science Laboratory, in the existing vacancy.

Anti-Corruption Bureau Director R. Jayalakshmi was transferred and posted as Inspector General of Police, CID Cyber Crimes. AP Special Police Battalions IG B. Raja Kumari was transferred and posted as IG, Railways, in the existing vacancy and given full additional charge as IG, CID Women Safety, until further orders.

Babujee Attada, DIG, Greyhounds, was transferred and posted as DIG, Technical Services, in the existing vacancy and given full additional charge as DIG, Greyhounds.

The government also appointed SPs for three new districts. Pankaj Kumar Meena, OSD, Polavaram, was transferred and posted as SP, Markapuram district, in the existing vacancy. Jagadeesh Adahalli was transferred and posted as SP, Palnadu district, while K. Chakravathi, SP, CID, was transferred and posted as SP, Polavaram district.

World.title: India needs multi-partisan approach for next level of development, says Manish Tewari
World.content:
Former Union Minister and Chandigarh MP Manish Tewari said taking India to the next level of development would require a multi-partisan approach, without which development would remain not just a challenge but a mirage.

He was addressing a gathering at the Indian School of Business (ISB) Leadership Summit 2026 in Mohali.

Mr. Tewari said time had come to put our money where our mouth was and that this required multi-partisanship. “Without it, in these polarised times, the grand project of taking India to the next level of development will remain not only a challenge but a mirage.”

“India needs a movement akin to 1991, when the then Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and his Finance Minister Manmohan Singh, who later became Prime Minister, forged a multi-party consensus on the country’s economic trajectory,” he said.

Economic betterment

He added, “A consensus which has held the field between 1991 and 2026 across different administrations. And that is what helped unlock the creative spirits, or the animal spirits, of the Indian economy and allowed it to grow. And as a consequence, the benefits went to a very large number of people who we were able to lift to economic betterment.”

Mr. Tewari, who was the keynote speaker, reflected on the larger questions of statecraft, global power and India’s place in an increasingly complex and changing international landscape. “Between 2019 and 2026, the world has changed spectacularly. And that is the reason that impelled me to write my latest book, which is called The World Adrift. As students of business, you cannot divorce yourself from the larger geopolitical construct which essentially characterises not only our daily work life but, more importantly, our very existence as a civilisation.”

The MP said, “Unfortunately, in the fourth industrial revolution technologies, we have not been able to really find our feet. And the reason is not that we don’t have talent, not because we don’t have the capacity to build capacity, but because we are not putting capital behind it.”

World.title: Ebola vaccine being tested in DR Congo outbreak zone
World.content:
Health workers in parts of the DR Congo, badly hit by a deadly Ebola outbreak, launched a test vaccination programme on Saturday (September 20, 2026) to see if jabs designed for a different strain of the virus could prove effective in this case.

The operation, backed by the World Health Organization and the Doctors Without Borders (MSF) charity, will see 20,000 frontline health personnel given the Ervebo vaccination in the Ituri and North-Kivu provinces, in a study lasting up to a year.

The current Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 3,639 people out of 7,541 confirmed cases, according to the latest figures from the country's authorities. That is a fatality rate of 48.3%.

It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is currently no approved vaccine or treatment.

The vaccination being rolled out as of this weekend was developed for use against the Zaire strain, and the study will determine how effective it might be against the Bundibugyo strain.

"We don't know to what degree it might be effective against the Bundibugyo strain," said Steve Ahuka, a Congolese official who is part of the health task force against the Ebola outbreak.

"It might offer a certain level of cross-protection against the Bundibugyo virus," said Nana Mimbu, an MSF research coordinator.

While WHO officials have cited "encouraging signs" that transmission may be slowing, MSF warned on Friday (September 18, 2026) that there was no clear evidence that the epidemic was coming under control.

WHO experts have said that early data on the Ervebo vaccine, notably from animal trials, suggested it could offer some protection in the current outbreak.

The UN health agency said last month that 70,000 doses of the vaccine, developed by the pharmaceutical company Merck and produced in Germany, were to be sent to the DRC.

AFP journalists on Saturday (September 19, 2026) saw health workers in Bunia, the main city of Ituri province, receiving vaccinations.

World.title: Nearly 300 participate in district-level Yogasana championship in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
The Visakhapatnam district-level Yogasana Championship was held at Yoga Village on Beach Road on Sunday, with nearly 300 students and yoga enthusiasts participating, according to the organisers.

The championship was organised by the Yogasana Sports Association of Visakhapatnam under the guidance of the Yogasana Sports Association Andhra Pradesh, affiliated to Yogasana Bharat.

Competitions were held in six age categories: sub-juniors (10-14), juniors (14-18), seniors (18-28), seniors A (28-35), seniors B (35-45) and seniors C (45-55). Participants competed in traditional yogasana, artist solo, artist pair, rhythmic pair and group categories.

Students from government, private and aided schools and universities across the district participated.

K. Ramesh Babu, Head of the Department at Andhra University’s Yoga Village, said practising asanas helped maintain physical health and mental stability. He advised children to practise asanas with dedication.

Durga Sai, K.A. Raju, DSP Prasada Rao, Chilaka Venkata Ramesh, Y.K. Prabhakar and Kiran Kumar served as directors of the event. Karibandi Ramakrishna and Raghavendra served as judges.

Organising member T.S.V. Prasada Rao said the first, second and third-prize winners would be sent to the State-level competitions to be held next month.

World.title: Supreme Court wants law to safeguard multi-crore court deposits
World.content:
A law is necessary to protect crores deposited by litigants across courts and tribunals in the country during pending appeals, the Supreme Court said in a recent judgment.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe observed that litigants’ money should be saved from ad-hoc management while calling for nationwide legislative reform to standardise how courts and tribunals handle money deposited during pending litigation.

The apex court pointed out the problem of the absence of uniform rules governing court-ordered deposits. For example, a court would direct a litigant to deposit money in order to get a stay while his or her appeal is heard out.

So far, individual courts and tribunals have passed orders on deposits and their investment during the pendency of appeals on a case-to-case basis. This, the court said, has left huge sums of money entangled in financial instruments across different banks, earning inconsistent interest rates and triggering post-judgment litigation over the interest-accounting of their deposits.

The Bench said the pressure of inflation and economic uncertainties also add to the anxieties about rates of interest on the deposits.

“In order to preserve the economic integrity of any deposit and to provide interest, there must be clarity and uniformity in the method and manner in which the deposit itself is handled. Lack of standardisation in the process by which sums deposited into the court are to be handled undermines this essential underlying principle of the time value of money as well as the accrual of interest in a certain and clear manner,” the recent verdict observed.

Further, the top court pointed out that the asymmetry in treating deposits made by litigants is leading to further pendency across courts.

“Lack of common standards and consistent principles are resulting in repeated determinations of routine questions concerning investment, renewal, quantum, accounting and interest on deposits, thereby increasing the burden on courts/tribunals,” the Bench, also comprising Justice Alok Aradhe, observed.

The court suggested the U.S. model of having a common platform where deposits made in courts and tribunals were pooled into one unified scheme and put into the most beneficial financial instrument for the litigating parties.

“This common platform will not only create certainty in the interest rates and increase the ease of accessibility for litigants but will also ease the burden on courts/tribunals regarding how this money deposited is to be invested and dealt with,” Justice Narasimha observed.

The apex court recommended a statutory framework modeled after international precedents, specifically pointing to the United States’ Court Registry Investment System (CRIS).

Justice Narasimha explained that federal courts across the U.S. were linked to the CRIS platform. The money deposited through the CRIS is automatically pooled into a single unified portal, which is used to purchase Government Account Series Securities. The centralised mechanism offers automatic interest accrual, transparency and liquidity.

“We are of the opinion that it is necessary to evolve and formulate suitable legislation on the subject. We request the Law Commission of India to examine the issues which we have highlighted and, in the process, also consider the laws which other countries have enacted. It may be necessary for the Law Commission to consult the Reserve Bank of India, Ministry of Finance and also the nodal Ministry of Law and Justice,” the apex court directed.

The Bench directed the judgment copy to be forwarded to the Law Commission chairperson; Governor, Reserve Bank of India; and the Secretaries to the Ministries of Finance and Law and Justice.

World.title: SIR notices to Jaishankar, Election Commissioner Sandhu, former CECs
World.content:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader L.K. Advani, Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, and former Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia were among several prominent names on Delhi’s draft electoral roll to be served notices either for “logical discrepancies” flagged by the Election Commission’s (EC’s) software or under the “no mapping” category.

Economist and Padma awardee Bibek Debroy, who died in November 2024, also figures in Delhi’s draft roll and has been flagged for “no mapping” with the previous Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll.

Notices are being generated to verify documents in cases of logical discrepancies in electors’ records and to establish eligibility in cases of “no mapping”. A list of those for whom notices were generated was published on Friday (September 18, 2026). It was reported on Saturday that Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, and former Union Ministers Kapil Sibal and Subramanian Swamy were among those on the list.

Debroy, who had served as chairman of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council and was 69 when he passed away, is listed as a 70-year-old elector in the Delhi Cantonment Assembly constituency in the draft electoral roll published on August 31, The Hindu has found. He has further been listed in the list of 33.1 lakh electors against whom notices have been issued. A notice was generated against his name because his record is unmapped to the previous SIR roll.

Also in the unmapped category were Mr. Advani, his daughter Pratibha Advani and daughter-in-law Geetika Advani.

Current and former election officials

A voter in Delhi Cantonment constituency, Election Commissioner Mr. Sandhu’s name was flagged for the “self-name mismatch” discrepancy, which means a mismatch between the name given during the current SIR process and the previous roll. The electoral registration officer (ERO) of the constituency later said in a press note that Mr. Sandhu’s name has been validated for inclusion in the final electoral roll after “documents, facts, and details” were verified.

Notices were also generated for two former Chief Election Commissioners (CEC) of India. Sushil Chandra and wife Neelu Chandra have been flagged for “no mapping with previous SIR”. The same reason was also given for former CEC Arun Goel’s notice. Mr. Chandra served as 24th CEC from 2021 to 2022, and Mr. Goel served from 2022 till he resigned from the role ahead of the general elections in 2024.

Other prominent figures

Mr. Jaishankar and his wife, Kyoko Somekawa Jaishankar, have also been flagged for notice for “no mapping” with the last SIR. For the same reason, former BJP IT cell head Amit Malviya has been issued a notice, while “self name mismatch” has been flagged in the case of his wife, Gauri Malviya.

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri’s name was also in the list under the “no mapping” category.

Several other prominent names also figure in the list. In the Jangpura constituency, sociologist and social psychologist Ashis Nandy, senior advocates Indira Jaising and Anand Grover, and political communications consultant Dilip Cherian were flagged for notices, all marked “unmapped with Last SIR”. Journalist Sheela Bhatt was flagged for a “self-name mismatch” and senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi for no mapping. In Kalkaji constituency, economist Deepak Nayyar was flagged for a “parent name mismatch”.

No reason given

While Mr. Sisodia and his family have been flagged for notices, no reason has been given for why he was on the list. For his wife, Seema Sisodia, “self-name mismatch” has been cited and “parent name mismatch” has been cited for their son, Meer Sisodia.

In the case of Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi, too, the slot for the reason his name was flagged was left blank.

There are at least 63,000 such entries in the list where the column for the reason for which notices were generated remained blank, as per analysis by The Hindu.

Mr. Sibal held a press conference over his and his wife’s names being flagged for notices, and said that his enumeration form was duly filled with his details from the 2002 SIR roll of Bihar and handed to the BLO. Despite this, the EC software has flagged him for being “unmapped with the last SIR”, he said.

Complaints

Delhi has, meanwhile, seen complaints from citizens who said their names were missing from the draft roll despite submitting enumeration forms, as well as cases of electors being wrongly marked “dead” or “shifted”. A total of 47.56 lakh voters have been excluded from the draft roll and placed in the ASDD (absent, shifted, dead or duplicate) category.

The 33.1 lakh electors flagged for logical discrepancies or no mapping constitute over one-third of the 97.5 lakh electors in the draft roll. Verification and disposal of these cases are to be completed by October 29, with the final electoral roll scheduled to be published on November 4.

The list also includes public figures such as former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar and his wife Sudesh Dhankhar, former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B. Lokur, Delhi Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh, former Delhi BJP president Virendra Kumar Sachdeva, historian Romila Thapar and New Delhi MP Bansuri Swaraj.

Electors in the “no mapping” category will have to establish their eligibility by submitting documents from the 12 documents prescribed by the EC for the verification process.

A senior election official said prominent leaders and other well-known personalities would not be required to visit hearing centres. Electoral Registration Officers will prepare a list of such cases and direct Booth Level Officers to visit their registered addresses to verify the records and resolve the discrepancies, the official said.

World.title: Two officers among 6 martyred, 8 terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR
World.content:
Two officers and four security personnel were martyred while eight terrorists were killed in a fire exchange in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district on Sunday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

During an intense fire exchange between a “security forces convoy and Khwarij”, 23-year-old Captain Abuzar Farooq from Gujranwala and 22-year-old Lieutenant Sheraz Babar of Chakwal, “who were leading their troops from the front, fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom along with their four men”.

On the other hand, “eight Khwarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell due to effective engagement by own troops”, the ISPR statement added.

The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

A sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other terrorist found in the area, ISPR said.

It affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm-i- Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation at all costs,” the military’s media wing stated.

More to follow

World.title: Aleema detained under MPO in Lahore ahead of PTI's Sept 27 protest
World.content:
PTI said on Sunday that ex-prime minister and party founder Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, had been detained by authorities, after the office of Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days.

The development takes place amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

The September 20 order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz had ordered the detention or arrest of Aleema and a man named Muhammad Ameer under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO).

The MPO ordinance allows the authorities to order detention and restrict judicial review of such orders.

“Their custody shall be placed under the superintendent, Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat, Lahore. They shall be at liberty to make a representation to the provincial government against this order,” the document read.

Police sources confirmed to Dawn that Aleema had been taken to the Kot Lakhpat jail.

Following the arrest, Aleema’s sister Noreen Niazi addressed a press conference in Lahore, flanked by her sister’s counsel Advocate Mudassir Umar.

Noreen claimed Aleema was “picked up” along with her driver after she left her residence on Saturday and they later learnt that Aleema’s vehicle was parked at a police station. Meanwhile, the lawyer said they had yet to receive official confirmation of her arrest.

Aleema’s son Shahrez Khan, in a post on X, alleged his mother “was abducted after leaving home this morning”.

“Our family has had no contact or news of her whereabouts,” he wrote, clarifying that Aleema was on bail in all cases against her in Lahore.

“We demand the government immediately disclose her whereabouts and ensure her safe return,” Shahrez wrote.

The DC’s order cited a letter by the Lahore capital city police officer. It said the letter referred to police reports that said Aleema and Ameer “are prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”.

According to the order, the reports also mentioned that the two had been involved in roadblocks and protests on May 9, 2023, when PTI supporters and workers took to the streets against Imran’s arrest.

“They motivated the workers to damage public and government property. Moreover, they are again mobilising the workers through social media and public meetings to create law and order situation, raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the government/institution in order to provoke and incite them,” the order read.

It said multiple cases had been registered against the two, declaring them “potential dangers to public peace and tranquillity”.

According to the order, the Civil Lines Division superintendent of police and district intelligence branch in-charge recommended their detention under the MPO for a 30-day period “in order to keep the law and order situation in the city intact”.

Describing the development as part of “pressure” ahead of the September 27 protest, Noreen said the date would be a “historic day” in what she described as a movement for Imran’s release.

“We are all part of this movement,” she told reporters, urging PTI supporters not to be afraid despite what she alleged was a crackdown involving raids on homes.

She called on people to come out “for their country and Imran Khan”, alleging that his brother was being kept in custody unjustly and was not receiving proper medical treatment.

“If they think that by arresting Aleema Khan we will be frightened, they are mistaken,” she declared.

Advocate Umar noted an MPO(3) order had been circulating on social media and purportedly named Aleema and Ameer. However, he said, the government had not yet officially acknowledged Aleema’s detention.

“We are working out a legal course of action against the arrest. The government should own the arrest so that we can seek legal remedy,” the lawyer said.

He claimed that police had already informed a court that Aleema was not involved in the Jinnah House attack case pertaining to the May 9 riots.

The lawyer further claimed that the MPO order appeared to have been issued after Aleema was taken into custody, and alleged that her arrest was linked to her being the sister of Imran Khan.

Soon after reports emerged of Aleema’s arrest, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan wrote on X: “We have clarified that our protest will be peaceful. Our objective is to peacefully struggle for the fulfilment of our constitutional and political demands; we don’t want any kind of clash or violence.

“Arresting Aleema Khan sahiba under the MPO in this situation is tantamount to fuelling violence and tension. We strongly condemn it.”

He called for an end to all such actions and demanded Aleema’s immediate release.

The party would soon present its strategy against such actions, he said.

Earlier, the PTI posted on X that Aleema had been “abducted” in Lahore from outside her home by the authorities. In another statement, the party termed the action a “cowardly and deliberate attempt to worsen the situation”.

“Who is responsible for shameful news coming out of Pakistan almost every day now?” PTI wrote in yet another post sharing a Reuters report on the arrest.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram demanded that Aleema be presented in court immediately.

“A sister is being punished for speaking up for her brother,” Akram alleged on X.

Imran’s son Kasim Khan, who has recently been speaking to international media about his father’s incarceration, wrote on X: “First they imprisoned my father. Now they are coming after his family.”

Assailing the government, he said, “The world cannot keep looking away from what is happening in Pakistan.”

Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) also condemned the arrest in a statement, saying the move was tantamount to crossing all limits of “state oppression and political revenge.

“The TTAP strongly condemns this step by the government, especially the Punjab government. This action exposes the Punjab government’s current oppressive system,” it added.

The opposition alliance said Aleema’s arrest would not be tolerated and demanded her immediate release.

“The Punjab government must realise that oppression, arrests and revengeful acts cannot resolve political differences,” the TTAP said, reiterating its demand for Aleema’s release, as well as that of other “political prisoners”.

Detentions ahead of protest

Aleema’s arrest follows a string of reported actions against the PTI in Punjab ahead of its September 27 protest.

District authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under MPO a week ago, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh.

Similar reports have come from Islamabad, where the PTI plans to march on the protest day. However, the government has vowed to stop the march, and the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

On Saturday, the capital police took into custody four PTI activists and workers.

A police officer told Dawn the activists were arrested under separate charges on a complaint lodged by a sub-inspector.

The police got information that the PTI workers were holding a meeting in connection with the planned protest at a property dealer’s office in the area of E-16. Subsequently, a police team was constituted for the raid and arrests.

The police claimed that the workers tortured the police team when they raided the meeting venue, besides tearing their uniforms and taking them hostage.

On Thursday, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said he was “released” after being briefly detained, with the party claiming he was held by Islamabad police.

Officers in the police and capital administration also said they have started preparations to counter the PTI’s countrywide protest. Authorities have placed hundreds of containers at the city’s entry points as the administration braces for protests.

World.title: JI launches protest march towards Islamabad against petroleum levy
World.content:
Jamaat-i-Islami launched its protest march towards Islamabad on Sunday, with party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

In the morning, Naeem addressed JI supporters at Karachi’s Cantonment Station before departing for Islamabad by train. As per an update at 7pm, the Naeem-led caravan had reached Tando Adam after making a stop in Hyderabad.

In his Karachi speech, the party chief said that a road caravan had also departed for the federal capital in addition to the “train march”.

He added that the rally would pass through Hyderabad, Landhi, Nawabshah, Rohri and Sukkur, adding that “we will invite our sisters to join us once we reach [Islamabad]”.

Rehman said the purpose of the march was to help relieve the burden on the least privileged.

“Instead of providing relief to the people, the government has decided that it would make the nation pay for its bad governance,” he added. “We demand that the levy extortion should end. Petrol prices would then reduce quickly and reach around Rs200 per litre. That’s when the economy could move forward.”

He said that the government had increased petrol prices more than any other state in the region. “The government wants to rob the common people in times of crisis,” Naeem claimed.

The JI emir said voicing complaints on social media was pointless, urging supporters to step out of their houses to protest the injustice.

“For the past 36-37 days, nationwide protests have been ongoing,” he said, adding that protests were currently under way in Hyderabad, Sukkur, Mirpurkhas, Larkana, Naushahro Feroze, Rawalpindi, Gujrat and various cities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“JI has mobilised entire Pakistan,” he said. “No hindrances can stop the protesters.”

“When we reach Islamabad, it’s not guaranteed that the situation would remain under control,” Rehman warned. If the government tried to suppress the movement, the situation would get out of control, he said.

The party posted on X that the “train march” led by Rehman would reach Rohri, Sukkur for a rally at 8pm. The protesters would depart for Multan on Monday.

The JI has been holding nationwide protests against the fuel levy, which is more than Rs100 per litre.
